Clinical Validation of the Nursing Diagnosis Risk for occupational physical injury (00402) among Healthcare Professionals: A Case-Control Study.
papers.abstract: Objective: To obtain evidence of the clinical-causal validity of the nursing diagnosis Risk for Occupational Physical Injury (00402) among healthcare professionals working in hospital settings. Method: Clinical-causal validation of the nursing diagnosis through a case-control study conducted at a University Hospital. A total of 158 healthcare professionals participated: 79 in the case group (with occupational physical injury) and 79 in the control group (without occupational physical injury). Statistical analysis was performed using bivariate and multivariate methods. Logistic regression and odds ratios were calculated to measure the effect of exposure between the groups. An association was considered when the risk factor presented a p-value <0.05 and an odds ratio >1. Results: Insufficient knowledge of biosafety standards was identified as a protective factor. At the end of the multivariate regression model, three risk factors (lack of technical skills, excessive stress, and exposure to repetitive movement activities) and one associated condition (regular use of sleep-promoting substances) were validated. At-risk populatiovans did not remain in the predictive model. Conclusion: Clinical validation provided strong evidence for refining the nursing diagnosis Risk for Occupational Physical Injury, demonstrating its applicability to clinical practice.

papers.title: Long-term Electroclinical Outcomes After Herpes Simplex Virus Encephalitis: A Single-Center Case Series.
papers.abstract: ObjectiveHerpes simplex virus encephalitis (HSVE) remains an important cause of severe sporadic encephalitis. Electrographic seizures and status epilepticus may be underrecognized during the acute phase, and their relationship with long-term outcome is incompletely defined. We aimed to describe acute EEG abnormalities and long-term seizure and cognitive outcomes in adults with HSVE.MethodsWe retrospectively reviewed adults hospitalized with HSVE in the neurology ward or neurological intensive care unit between 2013 and 2022. Demographic and clinical characteristics, MRI findings, routine or continuous video-EEG findings, antiseizure treatments, and long-term outcomes were obtained from electronic health records and the EEG archive.ResultsNine patients (7 men; age range: 30-77 years) were included. Altered mental status was the most frequent presenting feature, and 3 patients had clinical seizures at presentation. MRI abnormalities were bilateral in 4 patients. EEG showed lateralized periodic discharges in 5 patients, electrographic status epilepticus in 4, and electrographic seizures not meeting status criteria in 1. Median follow-up was 8 years (range: 4-13 years). No patient with available follow-up reported recurrent clinical seizures after discharge. Mood and/or cognitive complaints were present in 6 of 8 patients with evaluable long-term clinical data.ConclusionIn this neurologically selected HSVE cohort, electrographic seizures and status epilepticus were frequent despite clinical seizures being documented in only one-third of patients at presentation. Long-term clinical seizure control was favorable under continued antiseizure treatment, whereas cognitive and mood complaints remained common. Larger studies using systematic continuous EEG and standardized neuropsychological assessment are needed.

papers.title: Repairing the disruption of protein homeostasis ameliorates REM sleep dysfunction in mouse models of Huntington's disease.
papers.abstract: Although disruption of sleep behavior is prevalent across different neurodegenerative diseases, there is little understood about the molecular mechanisms that tie them together. To explore this relationship, we turned to the autosomal dominant disorder Huntington's disease (HD), which shares many features common to more prevalent sporadic diseases, such as abnormal protein accumulation, early cognitive changes, and cell type specific degeneration. Moreover, HD patients suffer from sleep disruption, which precedes the appearance of core clinical features of the disease. We have previously found that upregulation of selective autophagy can prevent the aberrant protein accumulation that is typical of HD and other disorders. Thus, given the robust modeling of HD, we performed sleep analysis in the presence or absence of the upregulation of selective autophagy, to test the hypothesis that the proteinopathy significantly contributes to sleep dysfunction. We found that HD mice display rapid eye movement (REM) sleep impairments and protein aggregation in sleep-related regions including the nucleus accumbens and amygdala. Augmenting selective autophagy in the brain slowed aberrant protein accumulation and ameliorated REM sleep deficits in HD mice. Taken together, these data suggest that the disruption of protein homeostasis may play a key role in sleep dysfunction and disease.

papers.title: Five-Year PAP Persistence, Adherence and Patient Follow-up After Implementation of Telemonitoring and Pay-For-Performance in France.
papers.abstract: Following an important increase in the number of patients treated with positive airway pressure (PAP) therapy in France, a new nationwide model combining telemonitoring and a pay-for-performance scheme was implemented in 2018. To provide a comprehensive overview of 5-year persistence and adherence to PAP therapy and healthcare utilization after the change in the PAP pathway and model. This real-world cohort included adults from France started on PAP in 2019-2023. Data sources included provider records (including daily PAP data) and national claims data. Costs were evaluated from the national payer perspective. A total of 84,550 patients (63.7% men, mean age 58.5 years, 53.6% with obesity, mean apnea-hypopnea index 40 events/h) were included; 95.7% used telemonitoring. 58,116 patients had paired claims data. PAP therapy persistence was 83.5% at 1 year, 68.4% at 3 years and 60.5% at 5 years. Main documented reasons for stopping PAP were issues with PAP treatment (54.9%), changes in treatment needs (9.3%) and death (7.0%). There was a dose-effect association between PAP adherence in the first 4 months and 5-year persistence. In the first year of treatment, on average, patients consulted with a general practitioner 6.66 times and with another medical specialist 2.53 times; over the same period home service providers delivered 4.0 interventions at home, 3.6 by phone and 2.8 masks. The number of provider interventions (logistic, educational and supportive) increased as adherence decreased. Mean yearly total cost per patient was €5,462: €1,526 (28%) for hospitalizations, €672 (12%) for disability pensions and sick leave benefits, €436 (8%) for the PAP device, consumables and service, and €415 (8%) for medical consultations. The proportion of adherent patients at 5 years was high, partly driven by the early discontinuation of patients with low adherence. Alongside intensive medical follow-up, HSPs delivered interventions at greater intensity for patients with low adherence, consistent with the objective of the nationwide telemonitoring and pay-for-performance model. However, solutions are needed for patients who have PAP-related issues and to further reduce the therapy termination rate.
papers.journal: Annals of the American Thoracic Society

papers.title: Time-Resolved Surface-Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy Profiling of Peripheral Blood Mononuclear Cells Reveals Convergent Immunosuppressive Remodeling in Glioblastoma.
papers.abstract: Systemic immune dysfunction is a hallmark of glioblastoma (GBM) progression and therapeutic resistance, yet rapid, minimally invasive methods for sensing dynamic immune-cell state changes remain limited. Here, we introduce a label-free surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) immune-sensing framework that uses peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) biochemical profiles as an accessible readout of GBM-associated systemic immunosuppression. Ag nanoparticle-decorated black silicon SERS substrates were used to profile PBMCs in GBM-PBMC coculture models representing early and progressed tumor-immune interaction states over 3-72 h. Multivariate spectral analysis, correlation-network mapping, pseudotime analysis, partial least-squares regression, and transfer learning were then used to define Raman-detected immune remodeling. SERS detected GBM-induced PBMC biochemical divergence within 3 h and resolved distinct intermediate remodeling trajectories that converged by 72 h into a shared immunosuppressive signature separated from astrocyte-interacted controls. Partial least-squares regression organized the PBMC spectra into a time-associated immunosuppression trajectory with strong predictive performance (R2 = 0.84). These results were corroborated by flow cytometry, which demonstrated reduced T-cell activation and time-dependent myeloid remodeling over the co-culture period. A ResNet-1D model trained only on the in vitro SERS dataset classified 6 independent GBM patient buffy coat samples as GBM-like with >99.9% confidence, and similarity analysis showed close correspondence between patient spectra and GBM-conditioned PBMC signatures. These results establish SERS-based immune-cell profiling as a label-free strategy for sensing and modeling GBM-associated systemic immune remodeling and support its further development for minimally invasive liquid-biopsy applications.

papers.title: Can Sleep Disturbance Mediate the Relationship Between Professional Quality of Life and Mental Health Among Nurses? A Mediation Model.
papers.abstract: To examine whether sleep disturbance mediates the relationship between professional quality of life and mental health among nurses. Understanding the complex interplay among mental health, professional quality of life, and sleep disturbance is essential for developing strategies to enhance nurses' psychological well-being. A cross-sectional, correlational study was conducted using a convenience sample. The sample consisted of 258 nurses working in Dubai hospitals, United Arab Emirates. Mental health, professional quality of life, and sleep disturbance were assessed using the Nurse's Workplace Mental Health Questionnaire, the Short Professional Quality of Life Scale, and the PROMIS Sleep Disturbance 8b Short Form, respectively. Mental health was strongly and negatively correlated with burnout and compassion fatigue, and weakly to moderately and positively correlated with compassion satisfaction. Mediation analysis showed significant positive direct and indirect statistical associations between compassion satisfaction and mental health, with sleep disturbance as the proposed mediator. In contrast, burnout and compassion fatigue had negative direct and indirect effects on mental health through sleep disturbance. Sleep disturbance partially mediated the associations between professional quality of life dimensions and mental health among nurses. The cumulative burden of professional quality of life is substantially associated with nurses' mental health. Sleep disturbance showed a significant indirect association between professional quality of life and mental health outcomes, underscoring the need to integrate sleep-focused interventions into programs designed to promote nurses' psychological resilience and well-being. Nurse leadership and ongoing evaluation of working conditions are essential to sustain healthy practice settings and improve outcomes for both nurses and patients. Healthcare organizations should foster supportive work environments that strengthen nurses' psychological resilience and well-being.

papers.title: Etiology and geographic variation in acute symptomatic seizure management: An international vignette-based survey.
papers.abstract: Acute symptomatic seizures (ASyS) account for nearly half of new onset seizures, but evidence guiding management remains limited. We aimed to characterize international variation in ASyS management across common etiologies. We conducted a cross-sectional, vignette-based survey through the International League Against Epilepsy national chapters (February to May 2025). Five etiology-based vignettes assessed clinical and electrographic ASyS scenario after ischemic stroke, traumatic brain injury (TBI), meningitis, hyponatremia, and alcohol withdrawal. Respondents who managed neonatal seizures completed a neonatal stroke vignette. We assessed antiseizure medication (ASM) initiation, duration after clinical ASyS, and continuous electroencephalography (cEEG) use. Interrespondent variability was quantified by normalized Shannon entropy (H'). Multivariable generalized estimating equations accounted for repeated responses. Among 963 respondents (92 countries), 62% recommended ASM initiation in clinical and 61% in electrographic ASyS scenarios. Overall ASM initiation variability was high (H' = .96), highest for alcohol withdrawal (H' = 1.0), followed by stroke (H' > .9), and consistently higher for electrographic than clinical ASyS. Etiology was the strongest driver of ASM initiation. Compared with stroke, ASM initiation odds were higher for TBI (odds ratio [OR] = 2.5, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 2.2-2.8) and meningitis (OR = 1.9, 95% CI = 1.7-2.2), and lower for hyponatremia (OR = .2, 95% CI = .2-.2) and alcohol withdrawal (OR = .5, 95% CI = .5-.6). Compared with Europe, initiation odds were higher in North America (OR = 2.7, 95% CI = 2.0-3.6), Asia-Oceania (OR = 2.4, 95% CI = 2.0-3.0), and Latin America (OR = 2.0, 95% CI = 1.5-2.7), but not Africa. These differences persisted after accounting for country income. Compared with stroke, the mean ASM duration was 3.2 months shorter for hyponatremia and .6 months longer for TBI. Alcohol withdrawal durations were polarized (41% discontinued at discharge; 20% continued >12 months). cEEG use was markedly higher in North America than Europe (OR = 11.3, 95% CI = 7.8-16.5). Among 291 neonatal respondents, 75% continued ASM beyond discharge. ASyS management varies markedly, reaching near-maximal heterogeneity in several common scenarios. Although etiology drives decisions, geography and provider characteristics also influence care, underscoring an urgent need for randomized trials and international consensus guidance to harmonize care.
authors: International League Against Epilepsy Acute Symptomatic Seizure Task Force

papers.title: Anxiety sensitivity as a transdiagnostic factor in paediatric chronic pain and sleep disturbances: a systematic review.
papers.abstract: This systematic review sought to highlight what is known about paediatric anxiety sensitivity (AS), chronic pain, and sleep disturbances, with the goal of improving theories on chronic pain and sleep and identifying novel areas for intervention. PubMed, SCOPUS, and PsycINFO were searched through June 2026. Inclusion criteria: samples aged 0-18, assessed AS in relation to either chronic pain, sleep, or both, and were accessible in English. Of the 26 articles that met inclusion criteria, nine examined AS and sleep and 17 examined AS and chronic pain. No articles examined all three variables in concert. Higher AS was associated with worse sleep quality and efficiency, longer sleep onset latency, and insomnia symptomatology. AS was also related to worse pain outcomes, particularly fear of physical arousal, and may relate to the development and maintenance of chronic pain. This systematic review highlights what is known about AS and sleep disturbances and AS and chronic pain in paediatric samples. No articles have been published examining these variables together. A theoretical model is proposed suggesting that AS may be an important target in clinical interventions with the goal of improving both paediatric chronic pain and sleep problems.

papers.title: Essential Oils From the Flowers of Callistemon viminalis (Myrtaceae): Circadian Variation, Chemical Profile, and Potential in the Control of Phytopathogens.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the influence of the circadian cycle on the chemical composition and yield of essential oils (EOs) from Callistemon viminalis flowers, as well as to assess their biological activity against the phytopathogenic fungi Botrytis cinerea and Colletotrichum gloeosporioides. EOs were obtained from fresh flowers collected at 12 a.m., 6 a.m., 12 p.m., and 6 p.m. of the same day and analyzed by gas chromatography coupled to mass spectrometry (GC-MS). The in vitro antifungal assay was performed using the disk diffusion method. The EO of C. viminalis showed yields between 0.32% and 1.84%. The major constituents of the EOs were eucalyptol, α-pinene, and α-terpineol for samples collected at 12 a.m., 6 a.m., and 12 p.m., and eucalyptol and α-pinene for flowers collected at 6 p.m. The EO of C. viminalis proved effective in reducing the mycelial growth of C. gloeosporioides and B. cinerea at 500 µL.mL-1.

papers.title: Sleep Related Breathing Disorders in Patients With MuSK Myasthenia Gravis, Compared to MuSK Negative Myasthenia Gravis.
papers.abstract: Autoimmune Myasthenia Gravis (MG) is associated with obstructive sleep apnea. Muscle-specific kinase antibody positive MG (MuSK-ab+ gMG) patients often have more bulbar weakness than MuSK antibody negative (MuSK-ab-) patients, but data comparing sleep-related breathing disorders is scarce. Utilizing the University of North Carolina Myasthenia Gravis Registry, 30 MuSK-ab+ generalized MG (gMG) patients (26 female, 4 male) were matched with 30 MuSK-ab- gMG patients for age, sex, and Myasthenia Gravis Foundation of America (MGFA) clinical class. Additionally, 30 MuSK-ab- ocular MG patients were matched for age and sex. Features of sleep-related symptoms, sleep diagnosis, polysomnogram findings, need for positive airway pressure (PAP) and chronic nocturnal supplemental oxygen were analyzed. Statistical significance was determined using Chi-square test with 95% confidence intervals and Student T test (p < 0.05). MuSK-ab+ MG patients had a higher prevalence of sleep related breathing disorders than the two comparative groups (Odds Ratio [Confidence Interval] 4.97 [1.39-17.82], 3.82 [1.15-12.71], respectively) and for obstructive sleep apnea in MuSK-ab+ gMG vs. MuSK-ab- gMG (4.33 [1.20-15.61]). MuSK-ab+ patients had higher rates of sleep related hypoventilation than MuSK-ab- groups (8.8 [1.01-76.96], 19.46 [2.18-2574]) and requirement for bilevel PAP and nocturnal supplemental oxygen (Odds ratio for both groups, 23.04 [2.63-3037], 23.0 [2.63-3037]). Our cohort suggests MuSK-ab+ patients are more likely to have sleep-related breathing disorders independent of MGFA class, age, and sex. Given the long-term health risks of sleep-related breathing disorders, we suggest clinicians perform routine sleep screening with a low threshold for in-laboratory polysomnography.

papers.title: Scalp high-frequency oscillations differentiate neonates with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy with and without electroencephalographically confirmed seizures.
papers.abstract: Hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) is a leading cause of neonatal seizures, but seizure detection is challenging when continuous electroencephalography (EEG) is unavailable and neonates undergo only a single routine EEG. Biomarkers derived from routine EEG may aid identification of neonates with seizures. We investigated whether scalp high-frequency oscillation (HFO) rates derived from the first eligible routine EEG (1) differentiate neonates with HIE with and without seizures; and (2) contribute to seizure classification alongside established clinical, neurophysiological, and imaging biomarkers. We retrospectively analyzed routine scalp EEG recordings from 33 term neonates with HIE (17 with seizures, 16 without), obtained at a mean postnatal age of 4 ± 3 days. The mean analyzed EEG duration was 38 ± 14 min in neonates with seizures and 36 ± 20 min in those without. HFO rates in sleep segments were quantified using a validated automated detector. Scalp HFO rates were significantly higher in neonates with seizures than in those without (.12 ± .11 vs. .03 ± .02 HFOs/min/channel, adjusted p = .02). An HFO rate threshold of .07 HFOs/min/channel optimally discriminated neonates who had seizures from those who did not (area under the curve [AUC] = .81). HFO rates did not differ significantly according to HIE severity, therapeutic hypothermia, antiseizure medication response, EEG background activity, or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) abnormalities. Multivariable models incorporating HFO rate, EEG background activity, and MRI findings showed discrimination (AUC = .92, 95% confidence interval [CI] = .69-1.00 for logistic regression; AUC = 1.00, 95% CI = .75-1.00 for random forest), with HFO rate as the strongest contributor to seizure classification. These findings support scalp HFO rate as a potential electrophysiological biomarker of seizure occurrence in neonatal HIE, complementary to EEG background assessment and MRI findings. Prospective studies are needed to determine whether HFOs can predict subsequent seizures.

papers.title: Strengths and weaknesses in epilepsy training across residency programs in Italy: A multicenter survey by the Italian chapter of the Young Epilepsy Section (YES-I).
papers.abstract: The objective of the study was to assess epilepsy-related services across Italian neurology and child neuropsychiatry residency programs, evaluate residents and early-career specialists' perceived strengths/weaknesses in epilepsy training, and identify unmet needs and expectations for improving residency programs and Young Epilepsy Section (YES)-Italy educational initiatives. A nationwide cross-sectional survey was conducted between January and April 2026 by a focus group of the YES-Italy Education Task Force. A structured questionnaire was distributed to neurology and child neuropsychiatry residents and specialists within 2 years of completing residency, assessing demographics, epilepsy-related services, self-perceived competencies, training strengths and limitations, and suggestions for improving residency curricula with YES-Italy educational activities. Descriptive statistics were used; group comparisons (neurology vs. child neuropsychiatry; residents vs. early-career specialists) employed the Mann-Whitney U test. The survey was completed by 150 participants. Epilepsy training was widely available (85.3%) but variable and often brief (<6 months). EEG training was mostly embedded within epilepsy rotation (32.7%), organized as a distinct brief rotation (<3 months; 33.3%), or not available (19.3%). Core epilepsy services were widely present (inpatient wards 82.7%; neurophysiology laboratories 93.3%), while other services were less common (such as epilepsy surgery). Marked variability in Status Epilepticus management emerged across centers. Participants perceived adequate competence for core clinical-diagnostic domains, but lower competence for EEG interpretation and complementary disciplines. Perceived competence was higher in chronic than in acute care. Child neuropsychiatrists reported greater competence in neuropsychology and genetics, neurologists in neuroimaging and acute management. Clinical rotations and multidisciplinary case discussions were major strengths, whereas lectures and direct teaching required improvement. Suggestions for the YES-I group highlighted improving EEG training, structured educational initiatives, access to courses, webinars, and scientific materials. This survey highlights substantial heterogeneity and weaknesses in Italian epilepsy training, particularly regarding EEG interpretation, complementary diagnostics, and acute management, underscoring the need for national standardization, multidisciplinary educational pathways, and strengthened educational initiatives.

papers.title: Processed Electroencephalography-Guided Total Intravenous Anesthesia in a Malignant Hyperthermia-Susceptible Child Undergoing Ventricular Septal Defect Repair: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: Malignant hyperthermia (MH) is a rare, life-threatening reaction to certain anesthetic medications that can occur during surgery. Managing an MH-susceptible child for congenital cardiac surgery is particularly challenging: cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB), with its attendant hypothermia and subsequent rewarming, can obscure the early signs of an MH crisis. Total intravenous anesthesia (TIVA) is utilized for MH-susceptible patients, but titrating anesthetic depth during CPB can be complicated, and processed electroencephalography (pEEG) has been studied sparingly in the pediatric cardiac population. We describe the anesthetic management of a two-year-old, 10.4-kg child with a likely pathogenic variant in the ryanodine receptor 1 (RYR1) gene who underwent ventricular septal defect (VSD) repair with CPB. A trigger-free environment was established, general anesthesia was maintained with a propofol-based TIVA technique, and anesthetic depth was monitored with a SedLine® brain function monitor (Masimo Corporation, Irvine, USA), using the raw electroencephalogram (EEG), spectral edge frequency 95 (SEF95), and density spectral array (DSA). The intraoperative course was uneventful, and no features of MH developed. This case illustrates the feasibility of pEEG-guided TIVA in an MH-susceptible child undergoing congenital cardiac surgery with CPB, and the value of interpreting the spectral display rather than a single index value during hypothermia and rewarming.

papers.title: White matter microstructure and hyperintensity burden in isolated REM sleep behaviour disorder.
papers.abstract: Isolated rapid eye movement sleep behaviour disorder represents a prodromal phase of α-synucleinopathy. Diffusion MRI provides in vivo markers of white matter microstructural properties, while white matter hyperintensities reflect cerebrovascular injury. However, their relative contributions to cognitive and clinical dysfunctions in patients with isolated rapid eye movement sleep behaviour disorder remain unclear. We analysed 168 polysomnography-confirmed isolated rapid eye movement sleep behaviour disorder participants from the North American Prodromal Synucleinopathy Consortium. Multi-shell diffusion MRI was used to derive metrics from diffusion tensor imaging (fractional anisotropy and mean diffusivity) and Neurite Orientation Dispersion and Density Imaging (tissue-weighted neurite density index and orientation dispersion index) across 39 white matter regions using a modified Johns Hopkins University white matter atlas. White matter hyperintensity burden was quantified from fluid-attenuated inversion recovery MRI. Using linear regression adjusted for age and sex, we compared white matter microstructure and hyperintensity burden between clinically impaired and unimpaired participants and examined associations with multiple cognitive and clinical domains, including global cognition, working memory, motor severity, manual dexterity, autonomic dysfunction, olfactory function, prodromal disease severity and daytime sleepiness. False discovery rate (FDR) correction was applied to account for multiple comparisons. In our sample (n = 168), participants with clinical impairment (n = 57) demonstrated higher white matter hyperintensity burden than unimpaired participants (n = 111) and showed limited microstructural differences, including lower fractional anisotropy in the superior fronto-occipital fasciculus and inferior occipital white matter and higher orientation dispersion index in inferior occipital white matter. After adjusting for white matter hyperintensity burden, only increased occipital orientation dispersion index remained statistically significant. Diffusion metrics showed widespread associations with digit span forward performance and autonomic dysfunction. In contrast, increased white matter hyperintensity burden demonstrated broader associations with poorer Montreal Cognitive Assessment scores, poorer digit span forward performance, lower Purdue Pegboard performance and higher Prodromal Synucleinopathy Rating Scale scores, indicating greater prodromal disease severity. Our findings highlight cerebrovascular white matter burden as an important correlate of clinical dysfunction in isolated rapid eye movement sleep behaviour disorder and underscore the need to consider cerebrovascular lesions when interpreting diffusion imaging markers in prodromal synucleinopathy.

papers.title: Low-dose aripiprazole for long COVID symptom management: A retrospective observational study.
papers.abstract: Long COVID (LC) is defined as the persistence of new or worsened symptoms for 3 or more months following acute SARS-CoV-2 infection, affecting multiple organ systems. Currently, there are no approved drugs for treating LC. We reported the effect of low-dose Aripiprazole (LDA) on the management of LC symptoms in a retrospective study. A retrospective study was done using electronic health records from 50 adult patients from the Stanford LC clinic with a history of SARS-CoV-2 and subsequent LC who received LDA between 5/2021 and 10/2023. LDA was prescribed with dose titration (0.1-2.0 mg oral daily). The assessment include 29 symptoms, (ii) severity of each symptom on the Likert-scale 1 (mild) to 5 (very severe), and (iii) the Functional Status Scale (FSS) from asymptomatic (level I), symptomatic without limitations (level II), symptomatic with reduced daily activity (level III), symptomatic with a struggle to perform daily activities (level IV), or incapacitated and bedridden (level V). An improvement was defined as a reduction in the ordinal scale (V, IV, III, II, and I) from higher to lower before and after exposure to LDA. A composite score of the severity of the seven most common symptoms (headache, fatigue, brain fog, unrefreshing sleep, sleep difficulty, post-exertional malaise, and lightheadedness) was calculated to assess the effect of LDA pre- and post-treatment, using Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Tests. Within the cohort of 50 patients, the median patient age was 46.5 years, 62% were female, and the mean body mass index (BMI) was 27.5 kg/m2 The median duration of symptoms was 566.5 days (range 153-1457). The FSS improved significantly from 3.78 to 3.28 (p = 0.001). There were no statistically significant differences in reductions in symptom severity, symptom count, or composite scores across the seven selected symptoms. Symptom duration before treatment, and course of the illness before and after the aripiprazole period did not significantly affect treatment associated changes. The median dose of Aripiprazole was 1 mg. Aripiprazole was generally well tolerated in our study cohort, with no severe adverse effects reported. In our cohort study, LDA was associated with improved FSS. These retrospective observational results suggest that LDA warrants further investigation in a randomized controlled trial as a therapeutic option for LC. Exploring the mechanism of action for LDA in LC may also provide new insights into pathogenesis.

papers.title: Promotion and economic considerations of domestic Vagus nerve stimulation within the Chinese three-tier epilepsy center system.
papers.abstract: Epilepsy affects approximately 10 million people in China, with about 30% developing drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE). Vagus Nerve Stimulation (VNS) is an established neuromodulation therapy for DRE. Domestic VNS devices completed clinical trials in 2014 and entered clinical use in 2016. This study synthesizes clinical outcomes, promotion pathways, and economic considerations of domestic VNS devices within the Chinese three-tier epilepsy center network established by the China Association Against Epilepsy (CAAE). This narrative synthesis integrates data from previously published multicenter prospective real-world studies, CAAE accreditation records, market research, and health economics literature. Clinical outcome data were derived from studies encompassing 124 adult and 87 pediatric patients with DRE across 86 epilepsy centers. A cost comparison between domestic and imported VNS devices was performed based on market data and implantation volumes from 2022-2025. In adults, responder rates (≥50% seizure reduction) increased progressively from 35.4% at 1 month to 76.6% at 12 months post-implantation, with seizure-free rates reaching 10.9%. In pediatric patients, according to the available follow-up data, ≥50% responder rates (combining seizure freedom, 75% reduction, and 50% reduction) were 43.4% at visit 2, 40.6% at visit 3, 56.6% at visit 4, and 55.8% at visit 5; seizure freedom rates ranged from 1.1 to 9.3% across visits. Significant improvements were observed in sleep quality (PSQI: 5.43 → 4.44), depression (NDDI-E: 6.49 → 4.83), anxiety (GAD-7: 7.15 → 4.95), and quality of life (QOLIE-31: 54.40 → 61.33). Adverse events were mild and transient, primarily voice changes (20.3%) and cough (8.6%). The three-tier network comprises 526 centers (45 Tier-3, 259 Tier-2, 222 Tier-1) with standardized protocols and telemedicine platforms. Domestic VNS demonstrates encouraging efficacy, favorable safety, and improvements in comorbidities in both adult and pediatric DRE populations within the CAAE three-tier network. The network provides a structured framework for standardized application. However, the evidence is limited by the uncontrolled design of the primary studies, short follow-up, and the absence of a formal cost-effectiveness analysis. Prospective comparative clinical and economic validation is warranted.

papers.title: Detecting sleep deprivation from running biomechanics using machine learning classification: a comparison between wearable and laboratory motion capture.
papers.abstract: Sleep deprivation is associated with impaired endurance performance and an increased risk of running-related injury. Previous research has identified alterations in running biomechanics following a single night of sleep deprivation under laboratory conditions. However, whether these biomechanical changes can be detected using wearable technology remains unknown. Twenty-one recreationally active runners completed submaximal treadmill running under both normal sleep and total sleep deprivation conditions in a randomized crossover design. Biomechanical features were extracted simultaneously using a full-body motion capture system and a trunk-mounted wearable sensor. Five machine learning classifiers were evaluated in two classification tasks: a within-subject task using paired recordings from the same individual, and a between-subject task performed without individual baseline data. Within-subject classification exceeded chance level (label-permutation testing, p < 0.05 ) for most models and both measurement systems, with best accuracies of 84% for the wearable sensor (Logistic Regression) and 81% for the motion capture system (Random Forest). These findings indicate that sleep deprivation produces a systematic and individually consistent biomechanical signature during running. In contrast, between-subject classification failed across nearly all models and systems, with accuracies remaining close to chance level (˜50%), suggesting that inter-individual variability obscures the sleep-deprivation signal in the absence of personalized baseline data. Both systems converged on temporal organization, loading-related variables, and stride-to-stride variability as the most discriminative feature domains. Contrary to expectations, the laboratory motion capture system did not outperform the wearable sensor. Together, these findings suggest that individualized, baseline-referenced monitoring may be important for detecting sleep-deprivation-related changes in running gait, and suggest that a single trunk-mounted wearable sensor may provide a practical solution for real-world monitoring when paired recordings are available.

papers.title: Knowledge, attitude and practice of patients with immune-mediated and inflammatory rheumatic diseases towards mental health and psychological interventions.
papers.abstract: Autoimmune rheumatologic diseases are chronic, recurrent conditions that often cause pain, disability, and high treatment costs. These disease burdens increase the risk of anxiety, depression, and sleep problems, yet many patients do not receive timely psychological support. Understanding how patients perceive mental health and psychological interventions, and how they act on these perceptions, is important for designing effective education and support strategies. This multicenter cross-sectional study was conducted in six hospitals in China between July and December 2023 and patients with immune-mediated and inflammatory rheumatic diseases were included. Demographic information and KAP scores were obtained using a self-designed questionnaire. A total of 672 valid questionnaires were collected, with 499 female respondents and a mean age of 44.86 ± 15.54 years. The mean KAP scores were 5.65 ± 4.812 (range: 0-18), 23.03 ± 4.125 (range: 6-30), and 18.41 ± 4.179 (range: 6-30). Multivariable logistic regression with an a priori confounder selection strategy showed that knowledge (OR = 1.133, 95% CI: 1.086-1.182, p < 0.001), attitude (OR = 1.115, 95% CI: 1.059-1.173, p < 0.001), and age (OR = 1.023, 95% CI: 1.008-1.037, p = 0.002) were independently associated with practice. Patients with immune-mediated and inflammatory rheumatic diseases demonstrated inadequate knowledge, positive attitudes, and inactive practice towards mental health and psychological interventions. Structural equation modeling indicated that knowledge was directly associated with attitude (β = 0.369, p = 0.001) and practice (β = 0.518, p = 0.001), with attitude also showing a direct path to practice (β = 0.202, p = 0.001). Patients with immune-mediated and inflammatory rheumatic diseases exhibit notable gaps in mental health knowledge, attitudes, and practices. These findings provide valuable empirical targets for future prospective research and highlight the potential need for tailored educational programs to support patient wellbeing.

papers.title: Neuroprognostication in unconscious patients after cardiac arrest: considering the time course of prognostic markers.
papers.abstract: Hypoxic-ischemic brain injury (HIBI) is a major determinant of outcome after cardiac arrest (CA) and accounts for approximately two-thirds of deaths in patients who remain comatose after return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC), frequently following withdrawal of life-sustaining therapy (WLST) based on an anticipated poor neurological prognosis. Accurate neuroprognostication is therefore crucial to identify patients with potential for neurological recovery while avoiding premature pessimistic predictions. Current guidelines recommend a multimodal approach integrating clinical examination, electrophysiology, biomarkers, and neuroimaging. However, neuroprognostication is inherently time-dependent: HIBI is a dynamic process, and the prognostic value of individual markers evolves substantially during the hours and days following CA. Some markers may provide relevant prognostic information early after ROSC, whereas others achieve optimal accuracy only after 24-72 h or later, as brain injury evolves and confounding factors progressively resolve. Thus, both the selection of prognostic markers and the timing of their assessment are critical to optimize prognostic accuracy. This review summarizes the temporal evolution of the prognostic performance of clinical examination, electroencephalography, somatosensory evoked potentials, biomarkers of brain injury, and neuroimaging after CA, and discusses how their integration according to optimal assessment windows may improve multimodal neuroprognostication and reduce prognostic uncertainty.

papers.title: Youth Correlates of Genetic Liability to Substance Use Disorders.
papers.abstract: Substance use disorders (SUDs) are moderately to highly heritable and develop in stages that typically begin in adolescence or young adulthood. The predominant use of cross-sectional adult samples to study SUDs and their genetic liability leaves it unclear whether their correlates may plausibly reflect predispositional risk and/or arise as a consequence of exposure. We conducted a phenome-wide association study (PheWAS) of polygenic scores (PGSs) for SUDs (i.e., problematic alcohol use, tobacco use disorder, cannabis use disorder [CUD], opioid use disorder [OUD], and a general addiction risk factor) in children ages 8 to 13 years (n European ancestry = 5556; n African American ancestry = 1584) enrolled in the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study. Up to 1697 phenotypes were examined across several domains, including mental health, substance use, physical health, cognition, and screen media. The PheWAS yielded 309 significant associations with the SUD PGS, particularly among mental health, sleep, screen time, and caffeine consumption phenotypes. Most associations remained significant in substance-naïve participants. The CUD PGS had the largest number of associations and was particularly associated with externalizing behavior in both genetic ancestry subsamples. OUD PGS associations were enriched for cognitive and neighborhood environmental phenotypes. Neuroimaging phenotypes (e.g., resting-state functional connectivity) partially accounted for associations between the SUD PGS and screen time phenotypes. Genetic liability to SUDs is expressed during childhood as potentially modifiable risk factors that could be targeted to attenuate its expression in adolescence and adulthood.

papers.title: Endothelial glycocalyx remodeling and galectin signaling in aging associated epilepsy.
papers.abstract: Physiological aging can alter the brain endothelial glycocalyx and blood-brain barrier (BBB), while experimental seizures independently engage galectin-3 (Gal-3) and inflammasome-associated inflammatory signaling. This narrative review critically examines whether these observations justify a shared mechanism in aging-associated epilepsy. Primary studies support endothelial mucin-type O-glycosylation as a determinant of BBB integrity and Gal-3 as a modulator of inflammation in selected seizure models. They do not establish that endothelial glycan remodeling changes Gal-3 binding or initiates epileptogenesis. We distinguish extracellular galectin-glycan recognition from intracellular inflammasome signaling and address the anatomical separation between parenchymal microglia and the luminal glycocalyx. Glycan elongation, ligand density, terminal modifications, and steric accessibility could alter binding in different directions; uniform exposure of galectin ligands cannot be assumed. Galectin-1 also has context-dependent protective and detrimental effects. We propose compartment-resolved experiments combining glycan measurements, cell-specific perturbations, BBB assessment, and longitudinal electroencephalography to test the convergence hypothesis.

papers.title: Functional characterization of the pheromone receptor OR67d within the genus Drosophila.
papers.abstract: Insects rely on chemosensory cues to mediate essential behaviors, including mate recognition. In Drosophila melanogaster, the odorant receptor OR67d detects the male-specific pheromone cis-vaccenyl acetate (cVA), initiating diverse behavioral responses. However, the evolutionary conservation and functional tuning of OR67d receptors across Drosophila species remain largely unexplored. Here, we characterize OR67d receptors from nine Drosophila species using phylogenetic analysis, transgenic expression, and electrophysiology. While most orthologs retained sensitivity to cVA, some exhibited broader tuning, responding to structurally similar acetates. Notably, D. bipectinata and D. navojoa responded to cVA despite not producing it, raising the possibility that cVA detection has been maintained independently of endogenous production, possibly as a heterospecific cue. Structural modeling revealed overall high sequence conservation yet identified variable regions within the putative binding pocket potentially underlying differences in ligand selectivity. These findings contribute to our understanding of pheromone receptor evolution and how chemical communication systems diversify across Drosophila species.

papers.title: Ageing and anaesthetic sensitivity: the role of inflammaging in the vulnerable surgical brain.
papers.abstract: Ageing surgical patients demonstrate increased vulnerability to anaesthetic agents, including heightened sensitivity, reduced drug requirements, and delayed emergence, and they are also at increased risk of postoperative complications such as delirium and haemodynamic instability. These phenomena are only partially understood and have traditionally been attributed to the global functional decline associated with ageing. However, emerging preclinical and clinical evidence suggests that inflammaging and related neuroimmune alterations, including peripheral macrophage activation, blood-brain barrier dysfunction, and immune-to-brain signalling, may also modulate anaesthetic response. This narrative review examines current evidence on anaesthetic sensitivity in older adults, the role of macrophage phenotypes in ageing, and the mechanisms by which neuroinflammation may alter neuronal excitability, synaptic function, and electroencephalographic markers of anaesthetic depth. It also reviews methodological approaches ranging from rodent models to biomarkers such as the cerebrospinal fluid to plasma albumin ratio and EEG-derived indices. Overall, the available literature supports a biologically plausible link between age-related immune dysregulation and altered anaesthetic sensitivity, while also suggesting that these same pathways may contribute to broader perioperative brain vulnerability, including postoperative delirium. Direct clinical evidence remains limited, however, and many mechanistic links continue to rely on extrapolation from preclinical models. Further integrative perioperative studies combining immunological profiling, neurophysiological monitoring, and pharmacodynamic modelling are needed to clarify how neuroimmune ageing influences anaesthetic brain sensitivity in older adults.

papers.title: Thermally provoked itch in atopic dermatitis: current evidence, knowledge gaps, and digital approaches to nocturnal scratching.
papers.abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic inflammatory skin disease in which pruritus significantly contributes to sleep disturbance, impaired quality of life, and the itch-scratch cycle. Heat, sweating, hot-water exposure, and nocturnal occlusion are frequently reported as itch-aggravating factors, although these exposures are biologically heterogeneous. This narrative review critically examines the current clinical relevance, mechanistic evidence, and objective monitoring of thermally provoked itch in AD. Thermosensitive ion channels, epithelial cytokines, neuropeptides, dermal fibroblast-derived artemin, and altered peripheral and central sensory processing provide a plausible framework for thermally provoked itch. However, the relative contribution of these pathways to heat-aggravated itch in humans remains incompletely defined. Digital monitoring technologies, including wrist-worn actigraphy, smartwatch-based algorithms, hand-mounted sensors, non-wearable systems, thermal imaging, acoustic sensing, and multimodal devices, are increasingly used to quantify scratch duration, frequency, intensity, and sleep-related patterns in real-world settings. These tools do not replace patient-reported outcomes, but they may provide an objective behavioral layer for assessing otherwise hidden nocturnal burden and monitoring changes over time. Future prospective studies should define heat-responsive clinical characteristics, standardize nocturnal scratch endpoints, validate digital measures across pediatric and adult populations, and jointly assess thermal and humidity exposure, skin temperature, itch, scratching, sleep, skin-barrier status, disease severity, and relevant confounders. Such studies are needed to determine whether thermal exposure independently predicts clinically meaningful nocturnal scratching and to establish the clinical value of digital scratch-monitoring endpoints in AD. Integrating mechanistic insights with objective monitoring may support more precise assessment and patient-centered management of AD.

papers.title: Patient-specific heart rate modulates developmental electrophysiology in transcriptomic-guided in silico models of pediatric human atrial cardiomyocytes.
papers.abstract: Cardiac electrophysiology adapts throughout pediatric development, driven by factors including age-associated ion channel expression changes and decreasing heart rate. Our prior transcriptomic-guided simulations of human atrial cardiomyocytes predicted developmental-associated changes in electrophysiology biomarkers at a fixed pacing rate, leaving the contribution of age- and patient-specific heart rate unresolved. In this study, we incorporated intrinsic heart rate into gene expression-guided computational models to predict the interaction between developmental maturation and pacing rate to shape atrial electrophysiology. Virtual patient-specific populations of atrial cardiomyocytes were generated from the right atrial cardiomyocyte gene expression data from 117 patients, spanning neonates to young adults. We simulated each population at pacing rates corresponding to each patient's intrinsic ECG-based heart rate and at fixed rates corresponding to the patient cohort minimum, median, and maximum. We also simulated each population at the patient's intrinsic heart rate in the presence of isoproterenol. Action potential and calcium transient biomarkers were quantified, and partial least squares regression assessed key biomarker dependencies. For intrinsic-rate pacing conditions, action potential duration at 50% and 90% repolarization increased with age, whereas early repolarization shortened; maximum upstroke velocity increased, resting membrane potential became more negative, and alternans prevalence decreased. Developmental differences persisted during fixed-rate pacing conditions, indicating that differences were not explained solely by the faster heart rates of younger patients. Notably, intrinsic-rate simulations exhibited stronger age associations for upstroke velocity and alternans than fixed-rate simulations. Further, isoproterenol induced age-dependent responses, with most notably opposite directional changes in action potential duration. Sensitivity analyses indicated that electrophysiological phenotypes arose from interactions among ionic conductances, calcium handling, age, and heart rate. Collectively, we find that pediatric atrial electrophysiology reflects both intrinsic developmental remodeling and rate-dependent modulation.

papers.title: Socio-ecological risk factors associated with different health-risk behaviors among Chinese adolescents: a cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: To explore the association between the level of socio-ecological risk factors and adolescent health risk behaviors, and to provide theoretical basis for reducing the occurrence of adolescent risk behaviors and improving adolescent behavioral problems. This cross-sectional study was conducted in Zhengzhou City and 3377 participants were enrolled. Perceived socio-ecological risk was measured using a validated 50-item questionnaire. Grounded in ecological systems theory, investigating the risk factors associated with adolescent health risk behaviors across individual, family, school, community, policy, cultural and chronosystem level. Health risk behavior outcomes including diet, physical activity, sleep duration and screen time on weekdays and weekends, drinking and smoking behaviors and then divided into healthy and unhealthy groups. Independent t-test, ANOVA and chi-square test were applied for descriptive group comparisons. Binary logistic regression was performed to estimate associations between multi-level perceived socio-ecological risk and health risk behaviors. Demographic covariates covered gender, only-child status, residential areas, learning period, parental education, family economic status, number of friends and study burden. After adjusting for confounding factors, compared with participants in the low-risk group for total socio-ecological risk, participants in the high-risk group showed positive association between irregular diet (OR: 4.021, 95% CI: 3.145-5.141), lack of physical exercise (OR: 1.779, 95% CI: 1.400-2.262), short sleep time (weekday: OR: 1.475, 95% CI: 1.059-2.056, weekend: OR: 1.287, 95% CI: 1.048-1.580), long screen time (weekday: OR: 1.399, 95% CI: 1.090-1.797, weekend: OR: 2.086, 95% CI: 1.678-2.592), smoking (OR: 3.964, 95% CI: 2.894-5.428) and drinking (OR: 3.662, 95% CI: 2.321-5.778) and high social-ecological risk. The higher the risk of social-ecological risk, the higher the risk of developing health risk behaviors. The results supported the importance of investigating health risk behaviors in adolescents and the health risk behaviors were associated with socio-ecological risk.

papers.title: Interoceptive-autonomic pathways in mood state transitions in bipolar disorder: a hypothesis-generating brief review.
papers.abstract: Bipolar disorder is typically described in terms of clinical states such as depression, mania, or hypomania, but bodily signal processing, autonomic regulation, and emotion regulation across these states have not yet been integrated into a single testable model. This review distinguishes cross-sectional correlates of mood states from longitudinal predictors of subsequent mood changes. It proposes a state-dependent framework linking sleep-circadian disruption, autonomic flexibility, interoceptive processing, and emotion regulation; the temporal sequence and causal contributions of these components remain unestablished. Cross-sectional findings describe concurrent associations, recovery studies characterize changes accompanying symptom resolution, and prospective studies inform temporal ordering and prediction; none alone establishes a mechanism driving mood-state transitions. This article discusses direct evidence from bipolar disorder, transdiagnostic evidence, and theoretical inference in a hierarchical manner, without equating HRV with interoception or treating altered interoception as a single pathophysiological mechanism of bipolar disorder. Finally, it proposes a research protocol comprising state-stratified heartbeat discrimination/signal detection tasks, HRV reactivity and recovery, sleep and activity rhythms, ecological momentary assessment (EMA), and longitudinal assessment of state transitions.

papers.title: Insomnia Modifies the Association Between Insulin Resistance and Incident Hypertension in Hispanic/Latino Adults: A 6-Year Longitudinal Study.
papers.abstract: We aimed to explore whether insomnia modifies the relationship between insulin resistance (IR) and incident hypertension (HTN) over a 6-year longitudinal period. To explore the longitudinal relationship between IR, insomnia, and HTN, we included data from 3300 participants over a 6-year follow-up period in a large Hispanic/Latino cohort. IR was defined using the Youden index to select the optimal homeostasis model assessment of insulin resistance cut‑point based on ROC curve analysis, while insomnia was assessed using the Women's Health Initiative Insomnia Rating Scale. Cox regression analysis was performed to assess the relationship between IR, insomnia and incident HTN. We found neither IR nor insomnia alone was associated with incident HTN, whereas IR combined with insomnia increased the risk of HTN by 39% (HR, 1.39; 95% CI, 1.05-1.85) after adjustment for potential confounders. Meanwhile, a significant interaction between IR and insomnia was observed (P = 0.045). Post-estimation linear combination analyses showed that IR was associated with a 60% higher risk of incident HTN among participants with insomnia (HR, 1.60; 95% CI, 1.16-2.21), but not among those without insomnia. Moreover, this synergistic association was significantly associated with incident HTN among men and participants younger than 42 years. This large, longitudinal study identified a significant longitudinal relationship that IR was associated with a higher HTN risk only among participants with insomnia, suggesting that coexisting insomnia may identify a subgroup particularly susceptible to hypertension.

papers.title: Striatal and orbitofrontal grey matter volumes are associated with cognitive event related potentials during associative learning task performance in male and female children and adolescents.
papers.abstract: The individual differences in gray matter volumes and event-related potentials may underlie variability in associative learning. However, little is known about the sex differences in these structure-function relationships across development. The current study investigates associations between local gray matter volumes and brain responses during associative learning task in children and adolescents aged 7-21 years. We hypothesized that gray matter volumes of the basal ganglia and prefrontal cortex would be associated with event-related potentials indices of associative learning, in a sex-dependent manner. Final analysis included 138 participants (68 females, 70 males). Participants completed an associative learning task with concurrent EEG event-related potentials recording. Gray matter volumes were analyzed within 5 a priori regions of interest, predominantly located in the basal ganglia vicinity and prefrontal cortex. In females, anterior N400 latency to Early-stage stimulus onsets was positively associated with gray matter volume in the left putamen/lentiform nucleus and to Late-stage stimulus onsets with gray matter volume in the subgenual anterior cingulate. Anterior P300 amplitude to Late-stage feedback presentation was positively associated with gray matter volume in the right nucleus accumbens/putamen and the right medial orbitofrontal cortex. Correlations involving the subgenual anterior cingulate and medial orbitofrontal cortex were significantly stronger in the female group relative to the male group. In males, anterior P300 amplitude to Early-stage feedback presentation was associated with gray matter volume in a left hippocampus/amygdala cluster, yet not significantly differently from females. In exploratory analysis, after accounting for total brain volumes, age was positively associated with the volumes of striatal and orbitofrontal regions in both sexes, with largely overlapping patterns. Therefore, findings support structure-function relationships linking gray matter volumes of striatum and orbitofrontal cortex to brain activity during reinforcement learning performance. Given that associative learning is an instance of reinforcement learning, its underlying neural processes are influenced by the structural development of striatal and orbitofrontal regions.

papers.title: A morning-type circadian chronotype is linked to a retinal microvascular complication of diabetes.
papers.abstract: To evaluate the association between circadian rhythm phenotype and clinical outcomes in patients with diabetic macular edema (DME). Retrospective observational study. Sidney & Lois Eskenazi Hospital in Indianapolis, IN, USA and Spring Mill Professional Building, Ophthalmology - IU Health in Indianapolis, IN, USA. A total of 160 patients diagnosed with diabetic macular edema. Chronotype distribution included 73 morning types, 64 intermediate types, and 23 evening types. Not applicable. Central foveal thickness (CFT), visual acuity (logMAR), glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), duration of diabetes, and number of intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) injections. We observed that the morning type was the most common chronotype (73/160), with evening types being the least common (23/160). CFT was significantly higher in morning types (320.1 ± 113.6 μm) than evening types (283.6 ± 57.7 μm; P = 0.0045). No significant differences were found in HbA1c or visual acuity. Morning chronotype was associated with increased retinal thickness in DME, suggesting circadian rhythm may influence retinal physiology independent of glycemic control.
papers.journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice

papers.title: The perioperative sensory-cognitive interface: multimodal neuroimaging of hierarchical network reconfiguration in perioperative neurocognitive disorders.
papers.abstract: Perioperative neurocognitive disorders (PNDs) are commonly attributed to neuroinflammation, cerebrovascular stress, anesthetic neurophysiology, and pre-existing brain vulnerability. These mechanisms identify important insults but do not fully explain how they become disturbances of attention, perception, memory, executive control, and fluctuating awareness. We examine whether changes at the sensory-cognitive interface help explain these symptoms, focusing on postoperative delirium (POD) and early recovery within the broader PND classification. The interface comprises distributed, bidirectional operations that transform sensory evidence into context-sensitive representations through thalamocortical routing, integration, attention, and association systems. The framework makes three testable predictions: sensory function should add explanatory value beyond frailty and brain burden; perioperative effects should vary across hierarchical levels and time rather than reflect uniform suppression; and within-person recovery trajectories should explain outcome better than isolated scans. Anesthetic state-transition studies show that primary sensory responses can persist while feedback, thalamic broadcasting, and distributed integration are disrupted, but whether these changes cause PND remains unproven. Direct perioperative MRI and EEG studies identify pre-existing dysconnectivity, altered sensory and association-network organization, abnormal slow-wave and auditory-feedback dynamics, and incomplete postoperative recovery; nevertheless, findings are heterogeneous and sensory-specific tasks remain uncommon. These observations are compatible with established vulnerability-perturbation models and suggest that symptoms may depend on which networks recover and when. Structural-functional connectivity (SC-FC) coupling is one candidate measurement, not an established biomarker or a requirement of the framework. Longitudinal studies integrating sensory phenotyping, domain-specific cognition, delirium surveillance, MRI, EEG, physiology, and molecular markers should test whether this framework adds reproducible value beyond vascular injury, diffuse arousal failure, and latent neurodegeneration.

papers.title: Anterior thalamic nucleus inputs to the retrosplenial cortex are unperturbed in the hAPP-J20 mouse model of Alzheimer's disease.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease is a neurodegenerative condition characterized by progressive loss of memory and general decline in cognitive function. Although research has traditionally focused on the hippocampus and entorhinal cortex, other regions important for memory and spatial navigation, such as the anterior thalamic nuclei and retrosplenial cortex, are also affected. The retrosplenial cortex is an important brain region for both memory and spatial navigation, and displays dysfunction in humans during prodromal phases of Alzheimer's Disease. The anterior thalamic nuclei provide a major input to the retrosplenial cortex, with loss of this input to the retrosplenial cortex causing a dramatic reduction in the expression of the immediate-early gene product c-Fos. The anterior thalamic nuclei to retrosplenial cortex connection may thus present a new target for therapeutic intervention in Alzheimer's Disease. Here, we set out to determine whether Alzheimer's-like pathology perturbed projections from the anterior thalamic nuclei to retrosplenial cortex in the hAPP-J20 amyloidopathy mouse model, using optogenetic activation of thalamic inputs combined with ex vivo patch clamp electrophysiology. We found that the retrosplenial cortex displayed an age-dependent decline in basal c-Fos activity, with no additional effect of amyloid pathology on c-Fos expression. At all-time points (3, 6 and 9 months) measured, we found no evidence of impairments in the synaptic strength or efficacy of the anterior thalamic nuclei projections to either granular or dysgranular subdivisions of the retrosplenial cortex. We conclude that, in the hAPP-J20 mouse model, this pathway is unaffected by amyloid-β overexpression.

papers.title: Nonlinear associations between physical activity, sleep quality, and psychological distress in university students: a cross-sectional interpretable machine learning study.
papers.abstract: Physical activity and sleep disturbance may have nonlinear, interrelated associations with psychological distress. Objective: To develop an internally validated prediction model and explore MVPA-distress nonlinearity and statistical interaction with sleep disturbance. A cross-sectional survey included 1,980 undergraduates from 68 classes at one university in Jiangsu Province, China. High-risk distress was defined as K10 ≥ 22. Development and internal testing used 48 classes (n = 1,386) and 20 held-out classes (n = 594), respectively; tuning used 10-fold GroupKFold. XGBoost was compared with logistic regression, support vector machine, and random forest. Test performance uncertainty was estimated using 2,000 class-level bootstrap resamples. SHAP patterns were examined alongside post hoc restricted cubic spline (RCS), interaction, and continuous-K10 analyses. XGBoost had a test ROC-AUC of 0.838 (95% CI 0.812-0.861), average precision of 0.692 (0.614-0.765), and Brier score of 0.124 (0.108-0.141). At a development-derived threshold of 0.28, sensitivity was 0.739, specificity 0.846, and positive-class F1 0.658. Calibration slope was 1.03 (0.81-1.28), and intercept was -0.04 (-0.22 to 0.15). Cluster-robust RCS testing suggested nonlinearity (p = 0.007), with greater uncertainty above approximately 500 min/week. The exploratory MVPA × JSS-4 interaction test yielded p = 0.024. In this single-university sample, XGBoost had the highest observed discrimination among the evaluated models. Nonlinear MVPA associations and statistical interaction with sleep disturbance warrant independent investigation. The results do not establish causal effects, an optimal activity dose, clinical utility, or generalizability to other universities.

papers.title: Linking event-related potentials and structural MRI in the aging brain.
papers.abstract: Aging alters both brain structure and electrophysiology, which can be measured non-invasively by structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and event-related potentials (ERPs). On average, gray matter declines steadily from early adulthood, whereas white matter increases into midlife before declining. With respect to ERPs, the well-established P300 response shows reduced amplitude and delayed latency from early adulthood onward. Few studies test whether structural MRI and ERP measures correlate within the same individuals, and those that do disagree over which tissue tracks which ERP change. While ERP changes are not coupled to structural changes in a fixed manner, atrophy in gray and white matter tissue correlate with ERP response decay, and a clear pattern of structure-function coupling emerges with age. This dynamic in turn is magnified by age and disease. Technological advances are now enabling structural MRI and portable ERP to be collected from the same individual in a single visit, with machine learning able to model the two modalities jointly rather than separately. While clinical cohorts have historically been the starting point, healthy normative data sampled across the adult age range represents the foundational baseline. Establishing this coupling directly is the critical first step toward integrating MRI and ERP as mutually informative rather than parallel measures of the aging brain. Accordingly, this brief review assembles the evidence as a conceptual framework for linking MRI and ERP changes in healthy aging to support preclinical detection of cognitive decline, now enabled through recent technological advances.

papers.title: The association between physical activity and academic procrastination among college students: the mediating role of self-efficacy and the moderating role of sleep quality.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to investigate the associations between physical activity and academic procrastination among college students within a cross-sectional framework while examining the mediating role of self-efficacy and the moderating role of sleep quality. A cross-sectional survey was conducted with 428 college students from universities in Shanghai. Participants completed the International Physical Activity Questionnaire-Short Form (IPAQ-S), the Academic Procrastination Scale, the General Self-Efficacy Scale (GSES), and the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Data were analyzed using the PROCESS macro in SPSS 26.0 to test a moderated mediation model, adjusting for demographic covariates, including gender, age, academic major, academic year, only-child status, and geographic origin. (1) Physical activity was significantly and negatively associated with academic procrastination (β = -0.127, 95% confidence interval [CI] [-0.223, -0.031], p < 0.05) and positively associated with self-efficacy (β = 0.200, 95% CI [0.103, 0.296], p < 0.001). Self-efficacy was concurrently and negatively associated with procrastination (β = -0.235, 95% CI [-0.330, -0.142], p < 0.001). (2) Self-efficacy accounted for a significant portion of the association between physical activity and academic procrastination, with a significant indirect effect of -0.047 (95% CI [-0.078, -0.019]), accounting for 27.01% of the total effect. (3) Sleep quality significantly moderated the association between physical activity and self-efficacy (β = -0.147, 95% CI [-0.236, -0.056], p < 0.01) and the direct association between physical activity and academic procrastination (β = 0.147, 95% CI [0.058, 0.236], p < 0.01). (4) Conditional process analyses revealed that the indirect effect via self-efficacy and the direct association with procrastination were significant only among students with average or good sleep quality, but not among those with poor sleep quality. The findings reveal significant concurrent associations among physical activity, self-efficacy, sleep quality, and academic procrastination. Self-efficacy partially accounted for the relationship between physical activity and procrastination. Crucially, sleep quality emerged as a critical boundary condition: the linkages between physical activity and reduced procrastination (both direct and indirect) were evident only when sleep quality was adequate. These results underscore the necessity of adopting a stratified approach in future interventions-targeting physical activity and self-efficacy for adequately rested students, while integrating sleep hygiene support for those with poor sleep-pending validation through longitudinal or experimental designs.

papers.title: Distinct tonic inhibition and its plasticity in hippocampal OLM and non-OLM somatostatin-positive interneurons.
papers.abstract: Extrasynaptic GABAA receptors (GABAARs) mediating tonic inhibition are critically involved in the regulation of neuronal activity, synaptic plasticity and hippocampus-dependent learning and memory. Tonic inhibition itself was found to undergo plastic changes but the description of this plasticity in distinct subclasses of hippocampal interneurons (INs) remains incomplete. In the present study, we combined whole-cell electrophysiology with morphological reconstruction of biocytin-filled neurons to investigate plasticity of tonic GABAergic currents, induced by brief (3 min) NMDA administration, in oriens-lacunosum moleculare (OLM) and non-OLM subclasses of somatostatin-positive (SST+) INs in the hippocampal CA1 region. We found that, under control conditions, tonic current density was significantly larger in OLM than in non-OLM INs. Brief NMDA receptor activation significantly enhanced tonic current density in a subset of non-OLM SST+ INs, distinguished as the upper-median in the cumulative distribution, whereas tonic current density in OLM cells showed no plastic changes upon NMDA treatment. Since in the hippocampus, GABAergic plasticity often involves α5-containing GABAARs (α5-GABAARs), we used the selective α5-GABAAR inverse agonist L-655,708 and found that NMDA treatment increased the relative contribution of α5-GABAARs to tonic currents in non-OLM INs. These data altogether demonstrate that, whereas non-OLM SST+ INs show lower tonic current density than OLM cells, the former subgroup is characterized by greater susceptibility to NMDA-induced changes in tonic current density and these plastic changes are associated with an increased contribution of α5-GABAARs. The presented observations suggest a clear functional specialization of non-OLM and OLM SST+ INs in the regulation of hippocampal network activity.

papers.title: Cross-subject EEG driving fatigue detection: early personal spectral reference and causal long-sequence residual encoding.
papers.abstract: In cross-subject electroencephalography (EEG)-based driving-fatigue detection, most existing decoders are designed around second-scale short windows, whereas fatigue is a slow drift; short-window spectral features provide little direct evidence of that slow drift, limiting fatigue decisions. More critically, each individual's spectral baseline level and fatigue-change pattern differ, so simply lengthening the window still leaves models struggling to predict across individuals from observed spectral features. This work aims to enable cross-subject fatigue decisions under shared parameters, without per-driver specialized models. We propose early personal spectral reference with causal long-sequence residual encoding: an early personal spectral reference is estimated only from a short session-opening spectral window; subsequent spectral observations are mapped into residual space; state-conditioned temporal modeling accumulates and updates a residual state over a long causal sequence; and fatigue is read out from the terminal state. On leave-one-subject-out binary classification of the Multimodal Phenotyping Dataset of Driving Fatigue (MPD-DF), five-seed (2026-2030) macro-averaged F1 is 0.655 ± 0.005 (0.660 at seed 2026), outperforming the best matched-protocol absolute-spectrum baseline (≈0.587). On continuous vigilance regression of the SEED Vigilance dataset (SEED-VIG) under a subject-LOSO protocol, root mean square error (RMSE) is 0.209 ± 0.005 under 5Bands and 0.200 ± 0.003 under 2 Hz, both below matched-protocol baselines. An early personal spectrum estimated from a short opening window can reduce interference from intrinsic individual spectral level in fatigue decisions and provides a practical premise for cross-subject fatigue decoding. Accumulating and updating residual state over a causal long sequence in residual space further improves cross-subject decisions. Under shared parameters without per-driver models, the framework outperforms matched absolute-spectrum baselines on both fatigue classification and vigilance regression.

papers.title: Cardiovascular health based on the life's essential 8: overall status and subgroup differences across sociodemographic characteristics in the Netherlands.
papers.abstract: Estimating the cardiovascular health (CVH) status based on the Life's Essential 8 (LE8) in the Netherlands and determine subgroup differences across sociodemographic characteristics. Data from 2022 were obtained from two sources. Data on the behavioural factors diet, physical activity, nicotine exposure, sleep, and the health factor BMI were obtained from Statistics Netherlands. Data on the remaining health factors blood pressure, lipids, and glucose were obtained from a national primary care register. Total and metric specific LE8 mean scores were calculated, standardised, and stratified by sex, and, if the data allowed, by age, education, income, and migration background. The mean LE8 score was 73.0/100, with 69.4 for behaviour factors and 76.5 for health factors. Individual metric scores ranged from 42.8 (diet) to 90.5 (physical activity). Women scored higher than men on all metrics except sleep and physical activity. Individuals with lower incomes or primary education had lower scores than individuals with higher incomes or tertiary education. No consistent pattern was observed across metrics by age and migration background, although characteristics in metric scores did vary. The CVH in the Netherlands is intermediate. Heterogeneity in the scores indicates the need for stratification and provides information to tailor interventions.
authors: Dutch Heart Foundation Cardiovascular Health Working Group (Appendix B)

papers.title: The Sv DC Field: Large-Scale and Hierarchical Functions Regulator.
papers.abstract: Large-scale dynamic reorganization of brain functional networks has been extensively revealed by functional magnetic resonance imaging, yet its direct electrophysiological basis remains unclear. In our prior research on epilepsy, we identified a distinctive electrophysiological phenomenon referred to as the slow-varying direct current (Sv DC, 0.01 to 0.5 Hz) field. This field demonstrates both the stability characteristic of a physical direct current and the slow-varying property of bioelectrical signals, enabling it to reflect the dynamic alterations in relative bioelectric field fluctuations. To further characterize its behavior across different functional states, we recorded intracranial electroencephalography from epilepsy patients implanted with depth electrodes during visual, motor, and language tasks. The Sv DC field exhibited large-scale convergence and suppression, accompanied by information transfer to other frequency bands, during these tasks. In visual functional areas, Sv DC field displayed rhythmic oscillations tightly coupled with gamma activity and increased power, whereas in nonvisual areas, Sv DC field power decreased significantly. During seizures, Sv DC field showed characteristic spatiotemporal spreading dynamics, a phenomenon consistently replicated in macaque monkeys, rats, and mice. These electrophysiological patterns suggest that the Sv DC field exhibits both large-scale cortical functional networks and region-specific modulations, potentially offering a novel understanding on dynamic organization of brain functional networks.

papers.title: Editorial: Bridging electrophysiological markers from preclinical to clinical neuropsychiatric research.
Development of personalized machine learning models for predicting panic attacks in college students.
papers.abstract: Panic attacks (PAs) are unexpected episodes of intense fear and anxiety, accompanied by cognitive and physical symptoms that significantly impair day-to-day functioning. This study proposes a machine learning approach to predict PA risk in the upcoming week in individuals across mental health conditions, enabling timely and potentially preventive mental health intervention. We evaluate the approach in a longitudinal sample of behavioral and physiological data collected using Oura rings from 39 college students over six months.
