We assessed multiple prediction algorithms applied within both personalized and generalized frameworks, fitting unique models for each participant and pooling data, respectively. Across all 39 participants, personalized models using logistic regression achieved a pooled PR AUC lift of 1.17 (95% CI: 1.05-1.25) over chance-level prediction (p = .035), whereas the generalized model did not differ from chance (PR AUC lift of 0.99; 95% CI: 0.90-1.08); in a direct comparison, personalized models outperformed the generalized model (lift ratio=1.18, p = .047). Performance varied across participants: when personalized models were grouped by unsupervised clustering of test-set PR AUC lift, models clustered as well-fit (n = 8) showed a pooled PR AUC lift of 2.26 (95% CI: 1.50-2.89) and models clustered as poor-fit (n = 31) a lift of 1.09 (95% CI: 0.98-1.17). Because these groups were defined by test-set performance, they describe observed heterogeneity and require validation in independent data. Together, our findings point towards the potential value of personalized modeling approaches and suggest that passively collected daily measurements of sleep, activity, and physiology may carry signal for predicting PAs, which could ultimately be leveraged to identify individually tailored lifestyle interventions to reduce PA risk.

papers.title: The association between depressive symptoms, physical activity, flow state, and resting-state EEG in college students.
papers.abstract: Exploring the correlations among physical activity, flow state, and resting-state EEG in college students with depressive symptoms. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 216 college students. Participants completed questionnaires assessing depressive symptoms, physical exercise, and flow proneness, followed by a 5-min resting-state EEG recording. Group differences and associations were examined using independent-samples t-tests, χ² tests, Pearson correlations, and regression-based serial mediation analyses. The primary mediation models were adjusted for sex and self-rated physical health, with unadjusted models reported for comparison. Physical exercise was associated with fewer depressive symptoms and greater flow proneness, and significant frontal EEG lateralization differences were observed between students with and without depressive symptoms. In the unadjusted mediation analyses, significant indirect effects were observed through Fp2/Fp1 δ- and α2-band lateralization and through the serial EEG lateralization-flow pathways. However, after adjustment for sex and self-rated physical health, the EEG-related indirect effects were no longer statistically significant in either the δ- or α2-band model. In contrast, the indirect effect through flow proneness alone remained significant in both adjusted models (Ind2), indicating that the flow-related indirect association was more robust to covariate adjustment than the EEG-related pathways. There is a close correlation among physical activities, EEG-specific indicators and the state of flow. However, whether the EEG-specific indicators play a mediating role remains to be further verified.

papers.title: Association of pre-treatment sleep characteristics with reproductive outcomes among women undergoing assisted reproductive technology: a retrospective cohort study.
papers.abstract: To investigate the associations between pre-treatment sleep characteristics and reproductive outcomes in infertile women undergoing assisted reproductive technology (ART) and to explore whether embryo development may represent a potential pathway linking sleep characteristics with cumulative live birth. In this retrospective cohort study, pre-treatment sleep characteristics before ovarian stimulation were assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). The primary outcome was cumulative live birth, while secondary outcomes included embryo developmental parameters. Associations with ovarian reserve indicators were also evaluated. Multivariable regression, restricted cubic spline, exploratory mediation, and sensitivity analyses were performed. In an analysis of 11,090 included oocyte retrieval cycles, women with very poor sleep quality had a lower 1-year cumulative live birth rate (CLBR) (RR = 0.927, 95% CI: 0.881-0.977, P = 0.004). Sleep duration of 5 to less than 6 hours significantly reduced both 1-year (RR = 0.788, 95% CI: 0.737-0.843, P < 0.001) and 2-year CLBR (RR = 0.798, 95% CI: 0.748-0.852, P < 0.001). Furthermore, severe impairment in sleep efficiency, severe sleep disturbances, and severe daytime dysfunction were associated with lower CLBRs (P < 0.05). Secondary outcomes showed that poor sleep quality, short sleep duration of less than 5 hours, and use of sleeping medication 1-2 times per week correlated with lower available embryo rates (P < 0.05). Very bad subjective sleep quality was associated with an increased slow-cleaving embryo rate and high fragmentation rate (P < 0.05). Restricted cubic spline analyses suggested non-linear associations between sleep characteristics and ovarian reserve indicators. Exploratory mediation analyses suggested that embryo development may partially explain the associations of very bad subjective sleep quality and mild impairment in sleep latency with CLBRs. Poor sleep quality was associated with lower cumulative live birth outcomes and poorer cleavage-stage embryo development among women undergoing ART. Exploratory mediation analyses suggested that embryo development may partially explain the observed associations between sleep characteristics and CLBRs. As a potentially modifiable factor, sleep characteristics may represent an important consideration in optimizing reproductive care, although further prospective studies are needed.

papers.title: Continuous chronic musculoskeletal pain and its associated sociodemographic, psychosocial, and behavioral factors among adolescents living in a socially vulnerable urban setting in northeastern Brazil.
papers.abstract: Chronic musculoskeletal pain is common during adolescence, yet evidence from socially disadvantaged populations in low- and middle-income countries remains limited. This study investigated the occurrence of continuous chronic musculoskeletal pain and its associated sociodemographic, psychosocial, and behavioral factors among adolescents living in a socially vulnerable urban setting in northeastern Brazil. An analytical cross-sectional study was conducted with 296 adolescents aged 14-18 years from five public secondary schools in northeastern Brazil. The study area was characterized by socioeconomic deprivation, a Human Development Index below 0.499, and high levels of violence. Musculoskeletal pain was assessed using the validated Presence and Impact of Pain in Kids questionnaire, with continuous pain lasting more than three months considered the outcome. Anxiety and depressive symptoms, sleep quality, physical activity, school bullying, family violence, self-rated health, healthcare provision, and daily smartphone use were assessed using standardized instruments and structured questionnaires. Bivariate analyses and multivariable binary logistic regression were performed to estimate crude and adjusted odds ratios. 31.4% adolescents reported continuous chronic musculoskeletal pain. In the final adjusted model, poor sleep quality was associated with higher odds of pain (aOR=2.49; 95% CI: 1.04-5.97; p = 0.041), as were anxiety symptoms (aOR=1.93; 95% CI: 1.02-3.63; p = 0.042). Each additional hour of daily smartphone use was associated with an 8.8% increase in the odds of pain (aOR=1.09; 95% CI: 1.02-1.16; p = 0.011). Continuous chronic musculoskeletal pain was reported by nearly one-third of adolescents attending public schools in a socially vulnerable urban setting. Its associations with anxiety, poor sleep quality, and longer smartphone use reinforce the multidimensional nature of adolescent pain. These findings expand evidence from an underrepresented Brazilian population and support context-sensitive approaches integrating pain, mental health, sleep, and everyday behaviors within school and primary healthcare settings.
authors: Rhanna Emanuela Fontenele Lima de Carvalho
Saiwori De Jesus Silva Bezerra Dos Anjos

papers.title: The relationship among burden, anxiety, and depression among caregivers of elderly patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: the chain-mediating effect of coping styles and social support.
papers.abstract: Although anxiety and depression are common among caregivers of elderly patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), previous studies have mostly examined caregiving burden, coping strategies, and social support separately, and studies on how these factors act jointly-particularly the serial pathway from burden to psychological distress-remain limited. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate whether negative coping strategies and social support serve as chain mediators in the relationship between caregiving burden and psychological distress, among primary caregivers of elderly patients with COPD. This was a cross-sectional study. A total of 240 primary caregivers of elderly patients with COPD, hospitalized in Ningxia, China, were recruited by convenience sampling between August 2025 and November 2025. Data were collected using a demographic questionnaire, the Zarit Caregivers Burden Interview (ZBI), the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS), the Simplified Coping Style Questionnaire-Negative Coping subscale (SCSQ-NCS), and the Social Support Rating Scale (SSRS). One-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) and Pearson correlation analyses were performed, and the chain mediation effects were estimated using the bootstrap method to test the proposed model. Among the 240 caregivers, the mean age was 53.13 years and 60.8% were female; the mean caregiving burden score was 71.00 (standard deviation [SD] = 11.70), and the mean total HADS score was 22.18 (SD = 4.45). Age, education, relationship with the patient, occupation, monthly income, number of chronic diseases, sleep quality, and health status were the main factors associated with caregivers' anxiety and depression scores. Anxiety and depression were positively correlated with caregiving burden and negative coping styles. The model results showed that caregiving burden directly and positively predicted anxiety and depression, and also indirectly predicted anxiety and depression through the chain mediation of negative coping styles and social support. Caregivers of elderly patients with COPD experienced a considerable caregiving burden along with anxiety and depression. Caregiving burden was directly associated with anxiety and depression and was also indirectly associated with them through serial mediation by negative coping styles and social support. These findings suggest that interventions to reduce maladaptive coping and strengthen perceived social support may help alleviate the psychological distress of these caregivers. Given that health literacy and care-related knowledge are generally limited among caregivers of patients with COPD, the future studies should examine whether such interventions remain effective when caregivers' health literacy is low.

papers.title: Clinical characteristics of 104 patients with cluster headache: a single-center cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: To analyze the clinical characteristics of patients with cluster headache (CH). Between January 2021 and March 2026, a total of 135 patients with suspected CH who first visited the headache outpatient clinic at Central Hospital of Dalian University of Technology (Dalian Municipal Central Hospital) for headache attacks were enrolled. After excluding 31 patients who did not meet the eligibility criteria (secondary headache or incomplete data), the clinical data of the remaining 104 patients were analyzed. (1) All 104 patients completed the follow-up, with a male-to-female ratio of 4.2:1, and 97.11% were diagnosed with episodic CH (eCH). (2) Depression and anxiety were significantly more prevalent in females (p = 0.004 for both), and Sleep disorders also showed a significantly higher prevalence in females (70.00% vs. 42.86%, p = 0.029). (3) Among male patients, right-sided attacks were the most common laterality (54/84, 64.29%), whereas among female patients, left-sided attacks predominated (14/20, 70%). Alternating bilateral attacks occurred exclusively in four female patients (20% of females). (4) A circadian pattern was observed in 82.69% of patients, and the predominant time of onset was the afternoon (12:00-17:00). (5) 7.69% (8/104) of patients experienced no autonomic symptoms; their accompanying features included agitation with nausea, agitation with phonophobia/photophobia, or agitation alone. This study provides a comprehensive analysis of the clinical characteristics, comorbidity patterns, attack features, and accompanying symptoms of CH in the Dalian region. It enhanced local physicians' awareness of cluster headache, which may help reduce misdiagnosis, shorten the time to diagnosis, and improve patients' quality of life.

papers.title: Variation in infant subcortical brain development from 6 to 12 months in Down syndrome.
papers.abstract: Down syndrome (DS), arising from Trisomy 21, is the most common genetic condition associated with intellectual disability. While smaller total brain volumes have been consistently observed in DS, no longitudinal neuroimaging studies have examined volumetric brain development in DS during infancy, a period of rapid neural growth when interventions may have the greatest impact. High-resolution T1- and T2-weighted images were acquired during natural sleep in a multisite longitudinal cohort of 44 infants with DS and 39 control infants without DS at ages 6 and 12 months. Neuroimaging data were harmonized to reduce batch effects, and a novel deep-learning, repeated-measures segmentation approach was applied to optimize neuroanatomical segmentations. Total intracranial volume (ICV) and bilateral absolute subcortical volumes (amygdala, caudate, hippocampus, pallidum, putamen, thalamus) were first directly compared in infants with and without DS at 6 and 12 months. Hierarchical linear modeling (HLM) evaluated longitudinal group differences for each structure, accounting for sex, gestational age, and laterality. Subcortical group differences estimated by HLM were also compared to group differences in total ICV. ICV in infants with DS was lower than controls at 6 months (12.6%; p< .001) and 12 months (16.3%; p< .001). Subcortical structures displayed a range of lower volumes (6.9%-13.1%; p's ≤.003) in infants with DS, although the caudate and putamen were exceptions. Caudate volumes were on average lower in DS but not significantly different from controls, while putamen volumes were on average higher in DS but not significantly different from controls, except for the right putamen, which was significantly larger (5.3%; p =.018) at 6 months. In HLM, ICV and all subcortical structures showed slower growth in DS from 6 to 12 months, except for the amygdala and putamen, which displayed similar growth rates to controls. DS-associated reductions in subcortical volumes were similar in magnitude to ICV, although 12-month caudate and 6- and 12-month putamen volumes were enlarged relative to ICV. Infants with DS exhibited substantially reduced ICV and widespread reductions in subcortical volumes and growth from 6-12 months. Across a range of volumetric differences, findings were most distinct in the basal ganglia, for which volume reductions were attenuated in the caudate, while the putamen was uniquely enlarged with comparable growth to controls. These observations support early regional specificity in the neural impact of Trisomy 21 and underscore the utility of infant neuroimaging to inform biologically based interventions and clinical trial readiness in DS.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

papers.title: Lesion-directed quantitative EEG after reperfusion therapy is associated with malignant cerebral edema and functional outcomes in acute ischemic stroke: a prospective exploratory cohort study.
papers.abstract: Ischemic stroke causes electrophysiological slowing within minutes which may precede detectable structural changes, making electroencephalography (EEG) a sensitive bedside marker of tissue at risk. Prior quantitative EEG (qEEG) studies often averaged bilateral or frontal activity, focused on thrombectomy, and were recorded at 24 h. We tested whether a lesion-directed alpha-to-delta ratio (lesion-ADR) within 72 h after reperfusion is associated with malignant cerebral edema (MCE) and functional outcomes. In a prospective single-center cohort of anterior-circulation ischemic stroke treated with intravenous alteplase (IV-rtPA), endovascular thrombectomy (EVT), or both, a 7-min EEG was obtained ≤72 h after reperfusion. Lesion-ADR was defined as the mean ADR of ipsilesional electrodes; the reperfusion-to-EEG interval (ΔT) was recorded. The primary outcome was MCE (midline shift ≥5 mm and/or decompressive hemicraniectomy). Secondary outcomes were favorable functional outcomes at discharge and 90 days (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] 0-2). Model discrimination was assessed using ROC analysis and AUC with bootstrap internal validation. Adjusted associations were assessed using parsimonious Firth penalized logistic regression models. Forty-nine patients were included. For MCE, the combined lesion-ADR + ΔT model achieved an apparent AUC of 0.888 (95% CI 0.765-0.960); bootstrap internal validation yielded an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.889. For discharge independence (mRS ≤ 2; n = 9), the ADR-only model showed an apparent AUC of 0.899. Lesion-ADR remained associated with favorable outcome after separate adjustment for admission NIHSS (OR 1.438 per 0.1-unit increase; p = 0.009) and reperfusion treatment modality (OR 1.367; p = 0.022). For 90-day independence (n = 13), the ADR-only AUC was 0.759 (95% CI 0.615-0.869) and the ADR-only model showed moderate discrimination for 90-day functional independence. The association with 90-day outcome was attenuated after accounting for admission NIHSS (OR 1.245 per 0.1-unit increase; p = 0.088). A brief lesion-directed ADR obtained within 72 h after reperfusion was associated with functional outcomes, while its combination with EEG timing showed encouraging discrimination for MCE in this cohort. These exploratory findings suggest lesion-directed qEEG may serve as a potential adjunctive biomarker after reperfusion therapy and warrant validation in larger cohorts.

papers.title: Development and validation of a risk stratification model for mild cognitive impairment among older adults with possible sarcopenia integrating traditional Chinese medicine constitution: a multicenter cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: Possible sarcopenia is associated with cognitive impairment among older adults, while mild cognitive impairment (MCI) represents an important window for early identification. Existing MCI assessment approaches may depend on neuroimaging, genetic testing, or biochemical biomarkers, limiting their use in large-scale screening. Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) constitution may provide accessible information on individual physiological and functional characteristics, but it has rarely been incorporated into MCI risk stratification. To develop and validate a machine learning-based risk stratification model integrating TCM constitution and conventional health-related indicators for MCI among older adults with possible sarcopenia. This multicenter cross-sectional study included 3,310 older adults with possible sarcopenia from ten tertiary hospitals in China and an independent single-institution external validation sample of 314 participants. The concurrent outcome was screening-defined probable MCI based on a prespecified Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) criterion. After a stratified 7:3 training-internal-validation split, data-dependent preprocessing parameters and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) feature selection were estimated using the training data only. Multilayer perceptron (MLP), gradient boosting decision tree (GBDT), support vector machine, K-nearest neighbors, logistic regression, and AdaBoost models were fitted using prespecified settings and evaluated using discrimination, classification, calibration, and decision-curve measures. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were used only to describe contributions to model output. Seven features were retained: educational attainment, sex, smartphone usage, Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index score, Patient Health Questionnaire-9 score, qi-deficiency constitution, and damp-heat constitution. The MLP showed the highest internal discrimination, with an AUC of 0.853 (95% CI: 0.827-0.878); its AUC was 0.799 (95% CI: 0.773-0.823) in the external sample. The internal and external Brier scores were 0.168 and 0.151, calibration intercepts were -0.07 and 0.18, and calibration slopes were 0.80 and 1.07, respectively. SHAP analysis ranked feature contributions to model output and was not interpreted causally. This cross-sectional screening framework integrated TCM constitution with conventional indicators to stratify the probability of current screening-defined probable MCI among older adults with possible sarcopenia. The single-institution external evaluation supports only limited transportability; prospective multicenter evaluation and, where needed, recalibration are required before clinical implementation.

papers.title: Human or Not? Prior Knowledge, Recognition of Virtual Identity, and Neural and Subjective Responses to a Hyperrealistic Virtual Influencer.
papers.abstract: Despite the growing popularity of virtual social media influencers (VIs), little is known about how knowledge and recognition of a VI's virtual identity are associated with neural and subjective responses. We investigated whether prior knowledge of virtual identity, recognition during viewing, or remaining unaware was associated with differences in brain activity and subjective evaluations. Twenty female college students viewed a 1-minute silent video featuring a hyperrealistic Korean virtual influencer while electroencephalographic (EEG) activity was recorded. Subsequently, participants completed subjective evaluations and retrospectively reported prior knowledge or recognition of the influencer's virtual identity. Exploratory analyses compared EEG changes from eyes-closed rest and five subjective evaluation composite scores across the three groups, with correction for multiple comparisons. After correction for multiple comparisons, neither the EEG analyses nor the subjective composite analyses yielded statistically significant group differences. Descriptive means varied across groups, but these imprecisely estimated patterns did not establish group differences. The findings underscore the methodological importance of distinguishing prior knowledge from recognition during viewing. Computers Are Social Actors and Uncanny Valley perspectives generate hypotheses for future time-resolved studies rather than mechanisms demonstrated by the present data.

papers.title: Alcohol and cardiovascular disease: inter-organ crosstalk, microvascular dysfunction, and cardiovascular ageing.
papers.abstract: Alcohol-related cardiovascular risk is being fundamentally reappraised. Observational associations suggesting cardioprotection with light-to-moderate drinking have been challenged by contemporary cohort analyses, Mendelian-randomization studies, biomarker-informed investigations, and updated public-health guidance. Uncertainty nevertheless persists at very low exposure levels and for selected coronary or all-cause outcomes. Alcohol is therefore best viewed as a dose-, pattern-, and host-dependent cardiovascular stressor. Acute or binge drinking, sustained heavy intake, chronic intake with episodic binges, and withdrawal produce overlapping but distinct phenotypes, including hypertension, atrial fibrillation, ventricular arrhythmias, sudden death, alcohol-associated cardiomyopathy, heart failure, stroke, and vascular disease. A systems-cardiology framework is presented in which direct myocardial injury, electrical instability, haemodynamic and autonomic stress, vascular and microvascular dysfunction, and disrupted inter-organ signalling interact. Ethanol and acetaldehyde toxicity, redox imbalance, microbial and inflammatory mediators, neurohumoral activation, and metabolic or electrolyte disturbances can impair endothelial signalling, mitochondrial energetics, excitation-contraction coupling, electrical stability, and repair. Pathway dominance varies across exposure patterns and susceptible hosts; coronary microvascular dysfunction may represent a convergence pathway rather than an obligatory mediator. Cumulative injury can diminish perfusion, contractile, electrical, autonomic, and exercise reserve. Alcohol-related cardiovascular ageing is proposed as a unifying cumulative phenotype encompassing mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative and nitrative stress, inflammageing, senescence, impaired repair, circadian and epigenetic dysregulation, fibrosis, and ventriculo-arterial uncoupling, although direct human evidence remains incomplete. Age, biological sex, genetics, comorbidities, sleep-circadian disruption, nutrition, medications, and polysubstance misuse may modify pathway dominance and reversibility. Structured exposure assessment and alcohol reduction or abstinence, when indicated, are actionable components of cardiovascular prevention and care.

papers.title: Epilepsy at the Airport.
papers.abstract: Limited data exists on which people, including those with epilepsy, are at increased risk of seizures during air travel and the contribution of specific travel-related triggers. We retrospectively reviewed attendances at our Epilepsy Rapid Access Clinic (RASC) over a 19-month period to identify patients presenting with seizures related to air travel. We also included patients identified by the epilepsy team who had not attended the clinic. Of 242 RASC attendees, nine patients (3.7%) had seizures associated with air travel. An additional nine patients were identified through other sources. All reported events were bilateral tonic-clonic seizures. Six (33%) patients had known epilepsy, of whom five had idiopathic generalised epilepsy (IGE). Four of these six patients had well-controlled epilepsy prior to the travel-related seizure relapse. Six (33%) patients were diagnosed with epilepsy after evaluation, including two with IGE. Twelve (67%) patients presented with seizures whilst awaiting departing flights, with a notable clustering around morning departures. Sleep deprivation was reported by 15 (83%) patients as a trigger. These findings suggest that patients with IGE may be at higher risk of seizures in these circumstances. The predominance of events in departure terminals, particularly before morning flights, highlights a potentially modifiable risk factor. Targeted counselling on modifiable risk factors may reduce risk and anxiety and should be incorporated into routine clinical care to support safer air travel. Thus, patients should be routinely educated about the potential of air travel as a seizure trigger.

papers.title: Longitudinal attendance trajectories across three academic years in English secondary schools: Putative predictors and associations with emotional difficulties.
papers.abstract: To identify longitudinal attendance trajectories across secondary education, examine factors associated with trajectory class membership and assess associations with emotional difficulties. Three years of linked #BeeWell survey and administrative data were analysed for 28,736 pupils aged 12-13 in 2021/2022 across 156 secondary schools in Greater Manchester, England. Piecewise latent growth mixture modelling identified attendance trajectories across nine consecutive terms. Multinomial logistic regression examined putative predictors of class membership across individual, family, school, peer and community domains. Emotional difficulties were modelled as a latent growth process. Consistently High (92.4%), Progressive Decline (5.1%) and Decline and Partial Recovery (2.5%) trajectories emerged. Socio-economic disadvantage was strongly associated with both sub-optimal (persistently absent) trajectories (ORs = 2.94-4.97), with dose-response effects for neighbourhood deprivation. Special educational needs were associated with greater odds while sufficient sleep, school belonging and minoritized ethnic group membership was associated with lower odds of both sub-optimal classes; good physical health was associated with reduced odds of Progressive Decline only. LGBTQ+ identity was not independently associated in fully adjusted models. Pupils following sub-optimal trajectories reported higher emotional difficulties at study outset (d ≈ .34-.41), with no differences in rates of change over time. Attendance trajectories are socially patterned and associated with multiple co-occurring vulnerabilities. Emotional difficulties differences existed at outset but did not widen, inferring underlying vulnerability rather than a cumulative process across the observation window. Evidence of partial recovery indicates improvement is possible. Putative predictors tested herein offer promising candidates for research into causal mechanisms.
papers.journal: The British journal of educational psychology

papers.title: Global Prevalence of Clinically Significant Insomnia Among Cancer Patients: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
papers.abstract: Clinically significant insomnia is associated with multiple adverse health outcomes in cancer patients. This study aimed to examine the global prevalence of clinically significant insomnia among cancer patients and to determine the moderators of the prevalence estimate. Literature search was conducted from inception to October 1, 2025, across 11 major electronic databases, including PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, Embase, PsycINFO, Cochrane Library, CINAHL, CNKI, Wanfang, VIP, and CBM. Methodological quality was evaluated using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) critical appraisal tool. A random-effects model was employed to calculate the pooled prevalence using Stata 15.0. Using the I2 statistic to assess heterogeneity, we also conducted subgroup analyses and meta-regression to identify its possible sources. On the basis of a total of 39 studies comprising 14,094 cancer patients, the pooled prevalence of clinically significant insomnia was 34.6% (95% CI: 27.2-44.1). A total of 25 studies were assessed as having a low overall risk of bias and 14 as having a moderate risk. Subgroup and meta-regression analyses identified country income level and sample size as significant determinants of the pooled prevalence. Our findings indicated a high global prevalence of clinically significant insomnia in cancer patients, highlighting the urgency to integrate sleep health management into routine oncology care to optimize their health outcomes.

papers.title: Spontaneous Parturition at Term Is Governed by Endogenous Circadian Rhythms Rather Than Geophysical or Meteorological Factors: A Historical Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: Pervasive folklore suggests that lunar phases and acute weather shifts trigger spontaneous labor onset and membrane rupture, contributing to heightened maternal anxiety and influencing labor ward staffing. We evaluated potential associations between astronomical lunar phases, barometric pressure fluctuations, and extreme heat events with spontaneous labor onset and premature rupture of membranes (PROM). A historical cohort study was conducted at an urban tertiary academic center (1998-2022), analyzing 21,538 spontaneous, singleton, term deliveries. Birth records were linked to regional hourly barometric pressure, Heat Index (HI), sunshine duration, and eight astronomical lunar phases. Primary outcomes were daily spontaneous delivery count, the timing of birth across the 24-h cycle, and the occurrence of PROM. Multivariable Poisson and logistic regression models were applied, controlling for maternal age, parity, and birthweight. Spontaneous births were uniformly distributed across lunar phases, showing no increase during the Full Moon compared with the New Moon (IRR 1.01, 95% CI 0.94-1.09, p = 0.698). Days characterized by significant meteorological variance (barometric drops > 8 hPa; IRR 1.01, 95% CI 0.98-1.04, p = 0.459) and thermal stress (IRR 1.00, 95% CI 0.99-1.00, p = 0.484) were not associated with delivery frequency. Lunar cycles did not influence PROM incidence (p = 0.771; Full Moon aOR 0.77, 95% CI 0.56-1.07). Conversely, spontaneous deliveries demonstrated a robust endogenous circadian rhythm peaking at midday (11:00 AM-12:00 PM), consistent across weekdays, weekends, and parity subgroups. Spontaneous delivery timing at term appears to be governed by an endogenous circadian rhythm (likely reflecting nocturnal labor onset) rather than extrinsic lunar or meteorological triggers. Antenatal counseling can reassure families that parturition is guided by an intrinsic biological cadence rather than ambient fluctuations, while perinatal resources should align with circadian demand.

papers.title: Effects of Ambulatory Blood Pressure Monitoring During Polysomnography on Sleep Indices and EEG Power.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) may disturb sleep during polysomnography (PSG), and the first-night effect (FNE) can complicate interpretation. We evaluated changes associated with ABPM and FNE across whole nights and individual measurements. Methods: This secondary analysis included 72 nominally healthy adults in a balanced two-night crossover, with ABPM on one randomly assigned night. Linear mixed-effects models estimated associations with PSG-derived sleep indices, a composite sleep quality index (SQI), and relative electroencephalographic (EEG) power. Analyses of individual measurements summarized EEG changes, sleep-stage transitions, and automated arousal detections. Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (BH-FDR) adjustment was applied within defined analysis families. Results: FNE and ABPM were associated with lower SQI (β = -0.049 and -0.051, respectively; both BH-adjusted p = 0.028). FNE was associated with altered sleep continuity and architecture, whereas ABPM was associated with higher light-sleep and lower N3-sleep percentages and higher whole-night relative theta power. In the Night 2 paired analysis, relative delta power was lower and relative alpha, beta, and gamma power were higher during ABPM than before ABPM (all BH-adjusted p < 0.01); the theta difference did not reach significance (BH-adjusted p = 0.0632). Of 655 eligible ABPM measurements beginning during sleep, 395 (60.3%) contained at least one arousal detection within the 2 min measurement window. Conclusions: These detections indicate temporal co-occurrence and do not establish that cuff inflation caused arousal. Concurrent ABPM and study-night order should be considered when interpreting PSG. An adaptation PSG night may be considered when feasible, as may cuffless blood pressure monitoring once its accuracy has been established for the intended setting.

papers.title: Beyond Motor Neuron Degeneration: Non-Motor Manifestations and Multisystem Involvement in Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis.
papers.abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a fatal neurodegenerative disease that primarily affects the motor system through the degeneration of motor neurons in the motor cortex, brainstem nuclei, and anterior horn of the spinal cord. ALS typically has a focal onset characterized by muscle weakness, followed by progressive spreading to other body regions, with respiratory muscle failure representing the main life-limiting complication. Median survival is approximately 2-5 years after disease onset. In addition to the well-established motor manifestations, non-motor symptoms are increasingly recognized and may occur in approximately 50% of patients. These include behavioral and neuropsychiatric disturbances, sleep disorders, sensory abnormalities, autonomic dysfunction involving the cardiovascular, gastrointestinal, and genitourinary systems, as well as metabolic and endocrine alterations. Recent evidence supports the concept of ALS as a multisystem disorder characterized by substantial clinical, genetic, and neuropathological heterogeneity. Nevertheless, non-motor manifestations remain less extensively characterized than motor symptoms and are frequently underestimated in clinical practice. This narrative review summarizes the current evidence on non-motor manifestations in ALS, discusses their potential underlying mechanisms and impact on quality of life, and highlights areas requiring further investigation. A better understanding and systematic assessment of these manifestations may contribute to a more comprehensive and patient-centered approach to ALS care.

papers.title: Effectiveness of Adding Neuromuscular Training to Conventional Physiotherapy in Adults with Patellofemoral Pain Syndrome: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Patellofemoral pain syndrome (PFPS) is associated with pain, functional limitation and impaired balance. This study investigated whether adding neuromuscular training to conventional physiotherapy provides additional benefit over conventional physiotherapy alone in adults with PFPS. Methods: In this single-blind randomized controlled trial (NCT06407414), 56 adults aged 30-60 years with PFPS were randomized to conventional physiotherapy alone (control) or conventional physiotherapy plus neuromuscular training, each performed three times per week for 12 weeks as a home-based program with physiotherapist follow-up every three weeks. The analysis was per protocol and included the 50 of 56 randomized participants (25 per group) who completed the trial. The primary outcome was the Kujala Patellofemoral Score. Secondary outcomes were pain (Visual Analog Scale, VAS), the 30-Second Chair Stand Test, the Y Balance Test, the International Physical Activity Questionnaire-Short Form (IPAQ) and, as an exploratory outcome, the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Results: After treatment, the neuromuscular training group had higher Kujala scores (median 77 vs. 65; r = 0.81, 95% CI 0.69-0.89) and lower VAS scores (r = 0.72, 95% CI 0.55-0.83), and performed better on the chair stand test (mean difference 2.60 repetitions, 95% CI 0.88-4.32) and IPAQ-walking; these differences remained significant after Bonferroni correction for 12 comparisons, although for the chair stand test this was not consistent in a supplementary change-score analysis. Y Balance Test values are reported descriptively only, because the groups differed at baseline and the analytical definition of the reported values (stance limb) could not be verified against the original records. Between-group differences in the other IPAQ domains and the PSQI were not significant and were inconclusive. Conclusions: Under the conditions of this trial, adding neuromuscular training to conventional physiotherapy produced greater short-term improvements in pain and function than conventional physiotherapy alone. No conclusion is drawn regarding dynamic balance, and the effect on sleep quality remains uncertain.

papers.title: Orexin-2 Receptor Agonists in Narcolepsy: Restoring the Missing Signal.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Narcolepsy type 1 (NT1) results from loss of hypothalamic orexin neurons. Selective orexin-2 receptor (OX2R) agonists now permit direct receptor-level restoration of deficient signaling, but recent broad reviews do not fully integrate the post-approval, trial-specific efficacy, prescribing, and safety evidence. This review asks what benefits and risks are supported by current data, which toxicities appear class-related versus molecule-specific, and how OX2R agonism should be positioned clinically. Methods: We performed a targeted narrative review of peer-reviewed human studies, major guidelines, trial registries, and regulatory documents updated through 16 October 2026. Peer-reviewed trials and regulatory sources were prioritized; conference- or sponsor-reported data were used only when peer-reviewed evidence was unavailable and were identified as provisional. Results: In the pivotal phase 3 trials, oveporexton produced placebo-adjusted improvements in MWT sleep latency of 13.8-20.1 min, ESS reductions of 8.0-9.8 points, and weekly cataplexy incidence-rate ratios of 0.25-0.38. Clinically important safety considerations include insomnia, urinary frequency/urgency, CPK elevations, CYP3A interactions, and measurable abuse potential. Alixorexton phase 2 data support OX2R agonism as a developing drug class, whereas firazorexton illustrates molecule-specific hepatotoxic risk. Conclusions: OX2R agonists are best described as mechanism-based pharmacological restoration of orexin signaling, not proven disease-modifying therapy. Their comparative clinical position remains uncertain because head-to-head trials with established therapies are lacking.

papers.title: Transcutaneous Electrical Acupoint Stimulation Combined with General Anesthesia in Minimally Invasive Surgery for Lung Cancer: A Randomized, Patient- and Assessor-Blinded, Sham-Controlled Trial.
papers.abstract: Background: We aimed to clarify (1) the analgesic efficacy of transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation (TEAS) combined with general anesthesia during minimally invasive lung cancer surgery and (2) exploratory neural network correlates of acupuncture-drug combined anesthesia. Methods: Eligible patients receiving general anesthesia for minimally invasive lung cancer surgery were randomly allocated to perioperative TEAS or sham-TEAS in this randomized, patient- and assessor-blinded, sham-controlled trial. Postoperative patient-controlled intravenous analgesia (PCIA) was administered. Outcome measures included postoperative visual analog scale (VAS) pain scores, sufentanil consumption via PCIA, and total/effective PCIA pump presses. Perioperative electroencephalography (EEG) was acquired using a 22-lead recorder, and brainwave power spectra were analyzed using Fourier transform. Repeated-measures analysis of variance (RM-ANOVA) was applied to serial postoperative VAS scores at 6, 24 and 48 h. Independent-samples t-tests compared cumulative sufentanil consumption at 6, 24 and 48 h postoperatively. Post hoc simple-effect comparisons were performed as exploratory analyses without multiplicity adjustment. The EEG sub-study was exploratory; false-discovery-rate (FDR) correction was used to control multiple comparisons across electrodes and frequency bands. Results: In total, 109 patients were randomized. A significant group-by-time interaction was detected for postoperative VAS scores (F(1.599,171.124) = 68.287, p < 0.001). Simple-effect analyses revealed lower VAS scores in the TEAS group at postoperative 6 h (mean difference -1.900, 95%CI -2.181 to -1.619, p < 0.001) and 24 h (mean difference -1.391, 95%CI -1.645 to -1.138, p < 0.001), with no between-group difference at 48 h (mean difference -0.066, 95%CI -0.320 to 0.187, p = 0.605). The TEAS group also exhibited reduced PCIA sufentanil consumption at 6, 24 and 48 h postoperatively, alongside fewer total and effective PCIA pump presses. After FDR correction, exploratory EEG analysis identified potential dipole-related power differences in the prefrontal, occipital, parietal (postcentral gyrus), temporal and diencephalic regions, predominantly within beta-band oscillations (14-35 Hz). Conclusions: These exploratory findings suggest that TEAS combined with general anesthesia may reduce postoperative pain and analgesic requirement. This potential benefit may arise from TEAS-mediated modulation of pain-related neural networks; however, the observed intraoperative EEG oscillatory differences are exploratory neurophysiological correlates and do not confirm causal mechanisms.

papers.title: Self-Organized Explainable Symbolic EEG Feature Engineering Using Directed Lobish and Previous-Next Pattern: A Proof-of-Concept Study on Dementia Classification.
papers.abstract: Objective: Dementia is a prevalent neurological disorder, and accurate detection is essential for timely intervention. This study aims to design an interpretable symbolic feature engineering framework for EEG-based dementia classification and to examine how its performance depends on the validation protocol. Methods: We used a publicly available EEG dementia dataset including Alzheimer's disease (AD), frontotemporal dementia (FD), and healthy controls. A self-organized explainable feature engineering (SOXFE) model was introduced with five phases: (i) feature extraction using Bipartite Channel Transformer (BCT) and Previous-Next Pattern (PNPat), (ii) feature selection via cumulative weight-based iterative neighborhood component analysis (CWINCA), (iii) explainable output generation using Directed Lobish (DLob), (iv) classification through an ensemble tkNN classifier, and (v) information fusion with combinational majority voting (CMV). Performance was evaluated with segment-wise 10-fold cross-validation, leave-one-subject-out (LOSO) cross-validation, and nested participant-grouped 10-fold cross-validation. Results: Segment-wise 10-fold cross-validation, which allowed segments of one participant in both training and test folds, yielded accuracies of 99.12-99.74%. Participant-independent accuracy was substantially lower: 51.19-63.81% for LOSO and 49.00-62.50% for nested participant-grouped validation at the segment level. Participant-level LOSO accuracy equaled the majority-class rate for dementia versus healthy controls (67.05%) and fell below it for AD versus FD (57.63% versus 61.02%). No exact McNemar comparison showed an accuracy advantage over the majority-class baseline. DLob outputs were produced as feature-level visualizations. Conclusions: The findings support the feasibility of interpretable, algorithm-derived symbolic feature representations. They do not establish reproducible disease-related EEG characteristics or clinical diagnostic utility. DLob outputs describe the channel transitions used by the model. Independent cohorts and stronger participant-independent performance are required before clinical application.

papers.title: BioTWavePat: An EEG-Based Mental Performance Detection Model.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: EEG-based mental performance classification requires participant-separated validation and traceable feature identities. Methods: BioTWavePat-XFE constructs five single-rhythm and 15 signed cross-rhythm channel-rank transition layers, uses four cumulative-weighted selectors and tkNN/IMV classification, and decodes retained identities with Directed Lobish. We compared Protocol A (whole-dataset feature and pooled-test outcome selection), Protocol B (training-fold outcome selection with Protocol A features), and Protocol C (all data-dependent steps restricted to outer training data). STEW and MAT used participant-wise LOSO. TMPD included all 55 participants in 54 identifier groups; two same-class participants sharing an identifier were withheld together. Results: Protocol A segment accuracies were 83.08% (STEW), 93.14% (TMPD), and 91.15% (MAT). Protocol C accuracies were 80.46%, 82.50%, and 74.65%, with balanced accuracies of 80.46%, 75.17%, and 64.15%, respectively. These are the primary estimates without the identified selection leakage under the stated participant-separated validation design. Conclusions: Whole-dataset selection inflated the original estimates, particularly for TMPD and MAT. MAT Protocol C performance was close to majority prediction. Directed Lobish exposes selected feature identities without establishing physiological connectivity, causality or biomarker validity.

papers.title: Predictors of Early Postoperative Seizures Following STA-MCA Bypass in Adult Moyamoya Angiopathy.
papers.abstract: Background: Postoperative epileptic seizures are a recognized complication after superficial temporal artery-middle cerebral artery (STA-MCA) bypass for Moyamoya angiopathy (MMA), but their determinants remain incompletely understood. We aimed to identify clinical, radiological, and perioperative factors associated with early postoperative seizures following adult STA-MCA bypass. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 75 hemispheric revascularization procedures performed in adult MMA patients between 2005 and 2023, with each operated hemisphere treated as an independent analytical unit. The primary outcome was the occurrence of at least one in-hospital postoperative seizure; the primary exposure was cerebral hyperperfusion syndrome. Univariate and multivariable Firth penalized-likelihood logistic regression was used to account for the small sample size and rare outcome. Results: Postoperative seizures occurred in 14 of 75 procedures (18.7%). Hyperperfusion was identified in 6 procedures (8.0%) and showed the strongest univariate association with seizures (OR 10.20), followed by diabetes mellitus (OR 6.05). Right-hemispheric procedures showed a protective effect in the univariate analysis (OR 0.24). In separate multivariate adjusted models, hyperperfusion (OR 10.28) and diabetes mellitus (OR 5.70) remained associated with postoperative seizures (OR 10.28 and OR 5.70, respectively). Pre-existing epilepsy, antiepileptic treatment, and preoperative EEG abnormalities were not associated with seizure risk. Conclusions: Early postoperative seizures after direct STA-MCA bypass in adult MMA were most consistently associated with postoperative cerebral hyperperfusion in our cohort, while pre-existing epilepsy and preoperative EEG abnormalities showed no statistically significant associations. Early recognition of hyperperfusion may support risk-stratified postoperative surveillance and individualized management.

papers.title: Efficacy of Transcutaneous Auricular Trigeminal Nerve Stimulation in Migraine: A Randomized, Participant- and Assessor-Blinded, Sham-Controlled Trial.
papers.abstract: Background: Migraine is a leading cause of disability worldwide. Transcutaneous auricular trigeminal nerve stimulation (taTNS) has emerged as a non-invasive neuromodulation approach targeting trigeminal pathways involved in pain modulation. Objective: To investigate the effects of taTNS on migraine pain intensity, sleep quality, disability, and Heart Rate Variability (HRV) in patients with migraine. Materials and Methods: This randomized, participant- and assessor-blind, sham-controlled trial included 102 participants who received taTNS (n = 51) or sham taTNS (n = 51). Active taTNS was administered bilaterally at 60 Hz, 250 μs, and up to 16 mA for 20 min, three times weekly for 12 weeks; sham stimulation used identical electrode placement at 0 mA. The primary outcome measures were migraine pain intensity (VAS), migraine-related disability (MIDAS) and sleep quality (PSQI); secondary outcomes included HRV, assessed using the standard deviation of normal-to-normal intervals (SDNN) and root mean square of successive differences (RMSSD). Results: At post-intervention, VAS and MIDAS scores were significantly lower in the taTNS group than in the sham-taTNS group (both p < 0.001), whereas PSQI scores did not differ significantly between groups (p = 0.870). RMSSD was significantly higher in the taTNS group than in the sham-taTNS group (p = 0.013), whereas the between-group difference in SDNN was not statistically significant (p = 0.187). Conclusions: Compared with sham stimulation, taTNS was associated with greater reductions in migraine pain intensity and migraine-related disability, but no significant between-group difference was observed in sleep quality.

papers.title: Treating Fatigue in Sarcoidosis-A Phenotype-Based, Treatable-Traits Approach.
papers.abstract: Fatigue is one of the most prevalent and debilitating symptoms in sarcoidosis, yet its mechanisms remain poorly defined and therapeutic responses are often unsatisfactory. Given its multifactorial nature and the limitations of uniform treatment strategies, there is a need for more structured and clinically actionable approaches. This narrative review summarizes current evidence on biological, behavioral, treatment-related and comorbidity-related contributors to sarcoidosis-associated fatigue and proposes an author-developed framework informed by the treatable-traits concept. Rather than defining mutually exclusive categories, the framework describes clinically recognizable fatigue patterns, including active inflammatory fatigue; treatment-related fatigue; comorbidity-related fatigue; sleep-related fatigue; neuropsychiatric, cognitive, pain and small-fiber neuropathy-related fatigue; deconditioning and lifestyle-related fatigue; and residual/post-sarcoidosis fatigue. The proposed approach emphasizes systematic identification and prioritization of one or more relevant treatable traits, followed by targeted intervention and reassessment. It is intended to support clinical reasoning rather than to serve as a validated classification. The framework integrates previously recognized contributors to fatigue into a structured clinical pathway and highlights areas in which direct evidence for fatigue-specific interventions remains limited. Prospective validation is required to determine its reproducibility, clinical utility and ability to identify patients who may benefit from trait-matched interventions.

papers.title: Propofol Target-Controlled Infusion with the Eleveld Model in Opioid-Sparing and Opioid-Free Anaesthesia: A Narrative Review.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: The Eleveld pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK-PD) model is among the most extensively validated general-purpose models for propofol target-controlled infusion (TCI). It includes a binary covariate for concomitant drug administration, commonly labelled as opioid use, which reduces elimination clearance (CL) and the volume of the second peripheral compartment (V3) in an age-dependent manner. This works well for conventional opioid-based anaesthesia but is less clear for multimodal, opioid-sparing regimens built around ketamine, magnesium sulfate, dexmedetomidine and intravenous lidocaine. This review discusses how these four non-opioid adjuvants may interact with Eleveld-based propofol TCI dosing. Methods: We conducted a structured, non-systematic literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE, the Cochrane Library and the MDPI full-text index between May and early August 2026, combining terms for the Eleveld model and propofol TCI with terms for each adjuvant and for pharmacodynamic endpoints (EC50, Ce50, bispectral index, propofol requirement). Studies without a propofol-specific endpoint were excluded from the adjuvant-effect analysis. Results: Dexmedetomidine reduced the propofol concentration required for defined clinical and electroencephalographic endpoints. Magnesium sulfate reduced propofol dose requirements to a lesser extent, although concentration-response data are lacking. Ketamine's interaction with propofol was additive rather than synergistic, and its effect on the bispectral index was dose-dependent. Lidocaine reduced propofol requirements mainly during surgical stimulation, a context-dependent effect distinct from a fixed hypnotic potency. Conclusions: The Eleveld model remains the best-validated general-purpose tool for propofol TCI, and its concomitant-drug covariate is a pragmatic, data-driven solution to a real gap in its source data. Clinicians should anticipate reduced propofol requirements with dexmedetomidine and, to a lesser extent, magnesium, interpret the processed-EEG response to ketamine cautiously, and expect lidocaine's sparing effect mainly under stimulation, while titrating to clinical and electroencephalographic endpoints. Dedicated covariates for these agents, informed by prospective validation in opioid-free regimens, represent a logical next step in the model's development.

papers.title: From CPAP Prescription to Long-Term Follow-Up: Care Pathway, Adherence, and Multidomain Treatment Outcomes in Obstructive Sleep Apnea.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Long-term continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) management involves both engagement with care and sustained treatment outcomes. We aimed to characterize long-term follow-up attendance, longitudinal adherence, and multidomain treatment outcomes in patients with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). Methods: We studied 172 adults with OSA who entered a real-world CPAP care pathway. Long-term attendance was evaluated among patients with ≥30 months of potential follow-up from CPAP prescription, with 24- and 36-month thresholds examined in sensitivity analyses. Longitudinal adherence and multidomain outcomes were assessed among patients with available follow-up data. Results: Among 114 patients in the primary long-term follow-up risk set, 80 (70.2%) attended; attendance was similar using 24- and 36-month thresholds (68.5% and 72.8%). Older age was associated with greater attendance (odds ratio 1.58 per 10-year increase, 95% confidence interval 1.10-2.28). Among 94 patients with paired adherence data, adherence according to available device-recorded nights was 78.7% at first and 79.8% at long-term follow-up, although 11.7% changed adherence category. At long-term assessment, device-recorded CPAP adherence, device-derived respiratory control (predefined residual apnea-hypopnea index [AHI] < 5 events/hour criterion), absence of residual sleepiness, and perceived treatment benefit were observed in 79.8%, 47.8%, 87.8%, and 89.3% of patients with available data, respectively. Among 71 patients with complete multidomain data, 45.1% simultaneously met all four predefined treatment-domain criteria, increasing to 63.4% using residual AHI < 10 events/hour. Conclusions: Care-pathway attendance and treatment outcomes represent distinct dimensions of long-term CPAP management. Similar aggregate adherence according to available device-recorded nights across assessments may conceal individual differences in adherence classification between observation intervals, while treatment outcomes are only partially concordant. Multidimensional reassessment may therefore identify clinically relevant discordance beyond adherence alone.

papers.title: Associations of Screen Time with Bedtime, Sleep, and Physical Activity Among School-Aged Children in Riyadh: A Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Evidence on screen use and sleep among younger children in the Middle East is limited. This study examined associations of screen time with bedtime, sleep duration, sleep quality, and physical activity among school-aged children in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Methods: In this cross-sectional study (September-October 2025), parents of 1208 children aged 4-15 years attending one private school completed an online survey. Associations were examined using chi-square tests, Goodman-Kruskal Gamma, and ordinal and binary logistic regression adjusted for age and sex. Results: The proportion going to bed at or after 22:00 rose from 7.4% among those with <1 h/day of screen time to 32.9% among those with >3 h/day, and the corresponding proportions not waking refreshed were 20.1% and 35.1%. Compared with >3 h/day, 1-2 h/day was associated with lower odds of late bedtime (odds ratio [OR] = 0.37, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.23-0.62) and non-restorative sleep (OR = 0.48, 95% CI 0.32-0.72), and estimates were stable across sensitivity analyses. The unadjusted association with shorter sleep (Gamma = -0.336) was attenuated after adjustment for age, and screen time was not inversely associated with physical activity. Conclusions: Higher screen time was associated with later bedtimes and non-restorative sleep, but not with lower physical activity, suggesting that sleep-focused guidance on evening screen use merits evaluation in longitudinal and intervention studies.

papers.title: Associations of Self-Reported Temporomandibular Disorder Symptoms with Sleep Problems, Perceived Stress, and Alexithymia in Young Adults: A Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: Background: Temporomandibular disorders (TMDs) are increasingly understood as chronic pain conditions in which biological susceptibility and psychosocial factors interact. Alexithymia, a personality trait characterized by difficulty identifying and describing feelings, has been linked to chronic pain; however, its relationship with self-reported TMD symptoms, perceived stress, and sleep problems in non-clinical young adults remains insufficiently explored. Objective: To examine the associations of self-reported TMD symptom severity with sleep problems, perceived stress, and alexithymia in young adults. Methods: In this cross-sectional online survey, 634 participants aged 18-40 years (74.3% female) completed the Fonseca Anamnestic Index (FAI), the 20-item Toronto Alexithymia Scale (TAS-20), the 14-item Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-14), and the Jenkins Sleep Scale (JSS). Group comparisons, Spearman correlations, and hierarchical multiple linear regression with FAI score as the dependent variable were performed. All analyses were re-run on the raw data during revision. Results: Self-reported TMD symptoms of any severity were present in 90.5% of participants. FAI scores correlated weakly to moderately with JSS (r = 0.40), PSS-14 (r = 0.37), and TAS-20 (r = 0.29) scores (all p < 0.001). After adjustment for sociodemographic variables (R2 = 0.147), sleep problems (β = 0.24), perceived stress (β = 0.16), and alexithymia (β = 0.14) explained an additional 14.6% of the variance in FAI scores (final R2 = 0.292; p < 0.001). Female sex, older age within the 18-40 range, and residence in an earthquake-affected province were also independently associated with higher FAI scores. Among the alexithymia dimensions, only difficulty identifying feelings was independently associated with FAI scores. Conclusions: In this young adult sample, self-reported TMD symptom severity was associated with sleep problems, perceived stress, and alexithymia, with weak-to-moderate effect sizes. Given the cross-sectional design and reliance on self-report, these findings reflect associations only-causal or temporal relationships cannot be inferred, and the findings support considering psychosocial factors when TMD-related symptoms are assessed.

papers.title: High-Flow Nasal Oxygen and Desaturation During Deep Sedation for Colonoscopy in Patients at Increased Respiratory Risk: A Propensity Score-Matched Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Hypoxaemia is the most common adverse event during procedural sedation. High-flow nasal oxygen (HFNO) may reduce desaturation through continuous positive airway pressure, anatomical dead space washout, and stable FiO2 delivery. This retrospective cohort study assessed the association between two oxygen delivery strategies-HFNO versus Venturi mask oxygen-and the incidence of desaturation (SpO2 <90% at any time) during deep sedation for colonoscopy in patients at increased respiratory risk. The two strategies differed simultaneously in flow rate, delivered FiO2 (0.50 vs. 0.40), device interface, and humidification; any observed difference cannot be attributed exclusively to the high-flow mechanism. Methods: A single-centre retrospective cohort study with propensity score matching (PSM) was performed, including 200 consecutive adult patients with established obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) or high-risk STOP-BANG criteria undergoing deep sedation for colonoscopy, grouped by oxygen delivery strategy: HFNO via nasal cannula (50 L/min, FiO2 0.50) versus Venturi mask (12 L/min, FiO2 0.40). The estimand of interest was the average treatment effect on the treated (ATT). Results: After 1:1 nearest-neighbour PSM (calliper 0.2 SD of the logit propensity score), 71 matched pairs were obtained; 10 of 17 covariates achieved adequate balance (SMD < 0.10). In the matched cohort, desaturation occurred in 12.7% of HFNO patients versus 22.5% of controls (matched-pair OR 0.53, 95% CI 0.23-1.23; p = 0.211; McNemar test), an absolute risk difference of 9.8 percentage points (95% CI -1.5 to +21.1). The estimate was imprecise and the confidence interval included no association. A sensitivity analysis using conditional logistic regression yielded an adjusted OR of 0.52 (95% CI 0.22-1.21; p = 0.129). The sample provided only 30.8% statistical power; an estimated 474 total patients (237 per group, parallel group design) would be required for 80% power in a future confirmatory randomised trial. Conclusions: In this propensity-matched cohort, the observed desaturation rate was lower with HFNO than with Venturi mask oxygen, but the estimate was imprecise, the confidence interval included no association, and residual confounding precludes definitive conclusions. These findings are hypothesis-generating and should be evaluated in a prospectively designed, adequately powered randomised trial.

papers.title: Relationship Between Combined and Individual Lifestyle Components and Stress Perception in Employees: A Cross-Sectional Study Focusing on Nutrition and Physical Activity.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Stress is one of the main concerns of the working population in Western countries, as it is associated with reduced well-being and performance, as well as the adoption of an unhealthy lifestyle. Nevertheless, scientific findings indicate that lifestyle improvements, particularly healthy nutrition and increased physical activity, are a pivotal tool for managing stress and improving well-being. This study aimed to verify, in a large cohort of employees, whether overall and individual lifestyle categories might be associated with different stress perceptions (primary outcome). Methods: In this cross-sectional study, 3380 employees from several Italian companies voluntarily completed an anonymous questionnaire on lifestyle. Five lifestyle components for which validated cut-offs are available in the literature (nutrition, physical activity, smoking, sleep, and body mass index [BMI]) were used to define lifestyle categories both individually and through a combined lifestyle score (overall lifestyle score [OLS]). Results: We observed that OLS healthier lifestyle categories are characterized by a progressive reduction in stress perception, which remains significant after adjustment for sex, age and job role (p < 0.001, ηp2 = 0.022). Moreover, they also showed lower fatigue and somatic symptom scores and better perceived health, sleep quality, and work performance. For individual lifestyle components, nutrition (p < 0.001; ηp2 = 0.011), physical activity (p < 0.001; ηp2 = 0.018), and sleep duration (p < 0.001; ηp2 = 0.015) were associated with stress perception, whereas findings for BMI and smoking were less consistent. Conclusions: Healthier dietary habits, higher physical activity volume, and a more favourable overall lifestyle profile were associated with lower self-reported stress in this population.

papers.title: Long-Term Add-On Use of a Fixed Multicomponent Formulation Containing Palmitoylethanolamide and Acetyl-L-Carnitine in Fibromyalgia Syndrome: A 15-Month Retrospective Single-Cohort Study of 150 Patients.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Long-term treatment options for fibromyalgia syndrome (FMS) remain limited and there is a lack of real-world data on the extended use of nutraceutical formulations containing palmitoylethanolamide (PEA) and acetyl-L-carnitine (ALC). This study describes a cohort treated for 12 months with a fixed multicomponent formulation containing PEA and ALC, followed by an additional visit three months post-treatment. Methods: This retrospective, uncontrolled single-cohort study involved 150 consecutive adults diagnosed with fibromyalgia syndrome (FMS). Participants received a fixed oral formulation comprising palmitoylethanolamide (PEA) 600 mg, acetyl-L-carnitine (ALC) 500 mg, Boswellia serrata 100 mg, vitamin B6 and vitamin E, administered twice daily as an adjunct to stable background therapy. Pain levels were assessed using the Visual Analogue Scale (VAS), and the impact of the disease was evaluated with the revised Fibromyalgia Impact Questionnaire (FIQR) over a period of up to 15 months. Sleep quality was measured using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) for up to 6 months. Missing data were addressed through various methods, including a mixed model, last observation carried forward, delta-adjusted and baseline-carried-forward scenarios, as well as non-responder imputation. Results: Sixty-four patients completed the 12-month course, 45 discontinued (36 for perceived lack of efficacy) and 41 were lost to follow-up. Estimated mean VAS fell from 76.3 to 52.3 at 12 months and FIQR from 73.6 to 56.1; under the worst-case assumption that every non-completer returned to baseline, the mean 12-month change in VAS was -13.0 points (95% CI -15.9 to -10.2). At 6 months, 78.1% of completers reached the FIQR minimal clinically important difference and 59.4% the IMMPACT 30% pain threshold, corresponding to 37.3% and 28.7% of all 150 patients with non-responder imputation; only 20.3% of completers (10.0% of all patients) improved by ≥3 PSQI points. Recorded adverse events occurred in 10.0% of patients. Retention at 12 months was 60.6% (42.7% if patients lost to follow-up were counted as discontinuations). In completers, pain and FIQR three months after the end of treatment were within one point of the 12-month values. Conclusions: In this uncontrolled cohort, 12 months of add-on treatment with a multicomponent formulation containing PEA and ALC was associated with reductions in pain and disease impact, whereas sleep outcomes changed minimally. However, attrition was substantial and partially response-dependent; therefore, the observed changes cannot be attributed to the formulation or its individual components. These descriptive findings support the need for a controlled trial with a duration of at least 12 months.

papers.title: The Circadian Diet in Age-Related Neurodegeneration: Nutrient Timing, Sleep, and Mitochondrial Mechanisms.
papers.abstract: Circadian rhythms coordinate sleep-wake regulation, endocrine secretion, nutrient handling and cellular energy metabolism. Circadian and sleep disturbances are associated with metabolic and cardiovascular morbidity and with neurodegenerative disorders, particularly Alzheimer's disease (AD) and Parkinson's disease (PD), although whether restoring circadian alignment modifies neurodegeneration remains uncertain. This narrative review examines chrononutrition within the broader context of sleep regulation, physical activity and circadian care, distinguishing evidence from cellular and animal models, observational studies and clinical trials. Meal timing and dietary composition act as signals to peripheral clocks, while NAD+, sirtuins and AMP-activated protein kinase link nutrient availability with clock regulation and mitochondrial metabolism. We appraise time-restricted eating, protein distribution, NAD+ precursors, tryptophan- and melatonin-containing foods, magnesium, omega-3 fatty acids, polyphenols and fermentable fiber. Experimental findings provide mechanistic plausibility, but metabolic improvements and target engagement have not translated into demonstrated neuroprotection. Clinical application must account for levodopa-protein interactions, undernutrition, frailty and sarcopenia. Adequately powered trials with circadian-phase assessment, controlled energy intake and clinically meaningful neurological outcomes are required before a "circadian diet" can be established as a disease-modifying intervention.

papers.title: Genetic Variants, Lifestyle Factors and Changes in Body Fat Percentage in Young Adults: An Exploratory Prospective Study.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: We examined whether eight obesity-associated polymorphisms and four lifestyle exposures were associated with changes in body fat percentage (BF%) in young adults. Methods: Eighty-four young adults of European ancestry (82% women; age, 20.5 ± 2.6 years) from Kazan, Russia, underwent bioelectrical impedance analysis at baseline and follow-up, 1.9 ± 0.8 years apart. A subsample was genotyped for eight obesity-associated polymorphisms (ADCY3 rs11676272, RERE rs301806, FTO rs1421085, TNRC6B rs4821940, PATJ rs12140153, TFAP2B rs734597, MMS22L rs9385223, and SLC22A3 rs9364554). Dietary intake and sleep characteristics were assessed using questionnaires, including the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Follow-up BF% was analyzed using ANCOVA adjusted for baseline BF%, follow-up duration, age and sex, with false discovery rate (FDR) correction for multiple testing. Results: Mean BF% increased by 1.61 ± 3.97 percentage points (pp) in men (p = 0.14) and by 0.25 ± 4.43 pp in women (p = 0.65), with wide inter-individual variation. Compared with participants in the bottom quartile (BF% change ≤ -2.45 pp), those in the top quartile (BF% gain ≥ 3.38 pp), i.e., those who gained more body fat, were more likely to carry the FTO rs1421085 T allele (p = 0.02; FDR q = 0.157), consumed fewer vegetables (p = 0.004; FDR q = 0.036), and had longer sleep duration (p = 0.028; FDR q = 0.126). Furthermore, poorer subjective sleep quality was associated with higher follow-up BF% in the whole cohort (β = 1.96 pp per PSQI point; 95% CI, 0.23-3.68; p = 0.027; FDR q = 0.11). Conclusions: Given the modest sample size and relatively short follow-up, few associations were detected, most of which did not remain significant after correction for multiple comparisons. Nevertheless, vegetable intake and sleep characteristics may be relevant to changes in adiposity during young adulthood.

papers.title: From Fasting to Caloric Restriction: State of the Art and Clinical Implications.
papers.abstract: Fasting and caloric restriction (CR) are central to current nutritional and metabolic research, although the complexity of physiological responses and their clinical applicability have yet to be fully elucidated. This review provides a state-of-the-art overview of fasting-based and CR-based interventions, including prolonged fasting, alternate-day fasting, semi-fasting, fasting-mimicking diets, and time-restricted feeding, with particular emphasis on their role in metabolic health. Mechanistically, these nutritional strategies modulate ketogenesis, autophagy, mitochondrial function, circadian biology, and nutrient-sensing pathways, including AMPK, mTOR, IGF-1, sirtuins, GCN2, and FGF21, thereby shifting cellular programs from growth and substrate storage toward stress resistance, repair, and metabolic flexibility. Current evidence supports beneficial effects of these nutritional interventions on body weight, adiposity, insulin sensitivity, inflammatory tone, and selected cardiometabolic risk factors. Evidence regarding neuroprotection, cancer prevention, and lifespan extension largely comes from preclinical studies, and the responses in humans are still unclear. This review also highlights the relevance of meal timing, refeeding, protein intake, and interindividual variability in shaping physiological responses and clinical outcomes. Overall, fasting and CR should not be viewed as a rigid protocol but as a personalized nutritional framework whose efficacy and safety depend on timing, duration, and patient context.

papers.title: Cannabinol for Sleep and Insomnia: A Critical Narrative Review and an Olive-Derived Polyphenol Combination Hypothesis.
papers.abstract: Cannabinol (CBN) is marketed for sleep, but its clinical evidence is limited and heterogeneous. This critical narrative review evaluates CBN-specific sleep studies and considers an olive-derived phenolic combination as a separate, untested clinical hypothesis. Three key randomized trials enrolled different populations and used oral doses of 20-300 mg over one night to four weeks. Primary sleep-quality or sleep-maintenance outcomes were not consistently positive; dose-ranging signals were multiplicity-sensitive and did not identify an optimal dose. At 300 mg, an acute insomnia trial reported selected secondary sleep benefits alongside next-day vigilance and simulated-driving concerns. Rodent findings implicate CBN and its metabolites, but route, exposure, tolerance and dependence limit extrapolation. Oleocanthal studies measured behavioral sleep in disease-model mice, whereas a human olive-phenol trial reported a fatigue benefit rather than a separately demonstrated sleep-domain effect. Parent phenolic instability, metabolism and uncertain target-site exposure weaken direct translation of micromolar assays. The proposed combination warrants exposure-informed investigation, not therapeutic endorsement. Progress requires product-specific safety and analytical qualification, component-controlled experiments and patient-prioritized outcomes alongside established insomnia care.

papers.title: Associations of Night Eating Behavior and Body Mass Index with Sleep Quality in Adult Women: A Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: Night eating behavior, adiposity, and poor sleep quality have been examined in previous studies, but additional evidence from large female samples with directly measured anthropometric characteristics is valuable. This study aimed to examine the associations among night eating behavior, body mass index (BMI), and subjective sleep quality in adult women, including their associations after adjustment for sociodemographic and lifestyle factors. This analytical cross-sectional study included 1203 women aged 18-65 years recruited from four family centers in Mamak, Ankara, Türkiye. Night eating behavior was assessed using the Night Eating Questionnaire (NEQ), and subjective sleep quality was evaluated using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Anthropometric measurements were obtained directly by the researcher. Correlation analyses and hierarchical multiple linear regression analyses were performed, with adjustment for age, education, occupation, smoking, alcohol consumption, and regular exercise. The mean PSQI and NEQ total scores were 5.58 ± 2.84 and 12.50 ± 5.04, respectively. Night eating behavior was moderately positively correlated with PSQI scores (ρ = 0.404, p < 0.001), indicating poorer subjective sleep quality at higher NEQ scores. BMI showed weak positive correlations with PSQI scores (r = 0.122, p < 0.001) and NEQ scores (ρ = 0.085, p = 0.003). In the fully adjusted regression model, NEQ remained significantly associated with higher PSQI scores (β = 0.425, p < 0.001), whereas BMI was not significantly associated with PSQI scores (β = 0.051, p = 0.115). Older age and current smoking were associated with higher PSQI scores, while regular exercise was associated with lower scores. The final model explained 22.9% of the variance in PSQI scores (adjusted R2 = 0.218). Night eating behavior was moderately associated with poorer subjective sleep quality and remained significantly associated with PSQI scores after adjustment for measured sociodemographic and lifestyle factors. Although BMI showed weak unadjusted associations with sleep quality and night eating behavior, its association with sleep quality was not statistically significant in the fully adjusted model. These findings highlight the relevance of night eating-related symptoms to subjective sleep quality in adult women, without establishing a causal relationship.
