papers.title: Sleep Quality, Psychological Inflexibility, and Work-Private-Life Interference in Relation to Emotional Exhaustion Among Ecuadorian Nursing Assistants: A Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: Evidence concerning emotional exhaustion among nursing assistants in Ecuador remains limited. This exploratory cross-sectional study examined associations of sleep quality, psychological inflexibility, and study-specific work-private-life interference with emotional exhaustion. The focus on emotional exhaustion as the sole outcome was selected during manuscript revision and was not prospectively prespecified. This analysis included 314 nursing assistants recruited through convenience sampling; 290 had calculable Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) scores and contributed to PSQI-dependent regression models. Emotional exhaustion was assessed using the nine-item Maslach Burnout Inventory subscale, psychological inflexibility using the AAQ-II, and work-private-life interference using three study-specific binary items. Ordinary least squares regression with HC3 heteroscedasticity-consistent standard errors was evaluated using Python (statsmodels). Of 290 participants with valid PSQI scores, 144 (49.7%) had scores above five. In the main model (R2 = 0.432), poorer sleep quality (B = 0.915, 95% CI 0.599-1.231), higher AAQ-II scores (B = 0.196, 95% CI 0.054-0.338), and greater work-private-life interference (B = 3.386, 95% CI 2.454-4.317) were associated with higher emotional exhaustion. Associations persisted after adjustment for age, sex, and shift work. In an exploratory model additionally accounting for concurrent depression, anxiety, and stress symptoms, the AAQ-II association was no longer statistically significant (B = 0.058, p = 0.400). Sleep quality and study-specific work-private-life interference were consistently associated with emotional exhaustion. The cross-sectional design, non-probability sampling, and exploratory analyses preclude causal or population-level inferences.

papers.title: Low Muscle Mass, Sleep Quality, and Quality of Life Among Older Chinese Adults: A Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: Background: Low muscle mass (LMM), poor sleep quality, and reduced quality of life (QOL) are common concerns in older adults. This study examined their cross-sectional associations and explored the statistical indirect association involving sleep quality, with particular attention to sensitivity to body-size adjustment and alternative model specifications. Methods: We analyzed data from 9366 adults aged 65 years or older in the 2018 Chinese Longitudinal Healthy Longevity Survey. LMM was classified using anthropometrically predicted appendicular skeletal muscle mass, while sleep quality and overall QOL were assessed using single-item self-reports. Regression-based indirect associations were estimated with 5000 bootstrap resamples. Sensitivity analyses examined alternative measurements, body-size adjustment, depressive symptoms, model ordering, missing-data assumptions, and sampling weights. Results: Anthropometrically estimated LMM was associated with poorer sleep quality (B = -0.066, 95% CI: -0.110 to -0.022) and lower QOL (total association: B = -0.073, 95% CI: -0.108 to -0.039). Better sleep quality was associated with higher QOL (B = 0.163, 95% CI: 0.147 to 0.178). The indirect association was small (B = -0.011, 95% bootstrap CI: -0.018 to -0.003) and attenuated after continuous body mass index adjustment (B = -0.001, 95% bootstrap CI: -0.010 to 0.008). Adjustment for depressive symptoms further attenuated the estimated indirect association, while a reverse-order model also yielded a non-zero indirect association (B = -0.020). Residual-confounding sensitivity analyses indicated dependence on assumptions about unmeasured common causes. Conclusions: Anthropometrically estimated LMM was associated with poorer perceived sleep quality and overall QOL, but the estimated indirect association involving sleep quality was small and sensitive to body-size adjustment, psychological covariates, and model specification. These cross-sectional findings do not establish a muscle-specific association independent of overall body size or a causal sleep-mediated pathway. Longitudinal studies incorporating directly measured body composition and validated multidimensional sleep and QOL assessments are needed to clarify these relationships.

papers.title: Loneliness and Mental Health Risks of Older People Living Alone in the Community: Cross-Sectional Study Protocol.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Some available evidence indicates an exponential rise regarding the proportion of older adults residing alone worldwide, which is associated with potential health and social risks, particularly those linked to loneliness and other mental health risk factors. This research aims to: (i) describe the physical and mental health profile of older people (aged over 65 years) living alone in the community, (ii) to examine the associations among the variables encompassing their mental health profile, and (iii) to explore the association between mental health and sociodemographic and health characteristics of this population. Methods: A cross-sectional study will be carried out. Potential participants must live alone in the selected municipality and be aged 65 years or older. Participants will be recruited through convenience sampling. Eleven instruments will be administered to participants assessing sociodemographic and health characteristics; fear of falling; sleep quality; frailty; anxiety, depression, and stress; loneliness; cognitive status; emotional literacy; perceived hope; functionality; and perceived social support. Data will be analysed using descriptive, univariate, and bivariate statistical methods. The study and its protocol were reviewed and approved by the Ethics Committee of a major public university in Northern Portugal (CEICVS 067/2022). Expected Results: This study aims to assess the physical and mental health of older adults living alone in a selected municipality in Northern Portugal, an area where such comprehensive data remain scarce. By conducting this analysis, we intend to inform and support the development of a highly personalized, evidence-based action plan, ultimately contributing to the mitigation of mental risk factors in this population.
authors: Maria do Perpétuo S S Nóbrega

papers.title: Nature, Characteristics, and Reported Experiences of Medical Malpractice Disputes Among Egyptian Physicians Practicing in Egypt and Other Arab Countries: A Cross-Sectional Medicolegal Analysis of Psychological Distress, Somatic Symptoms, and Defensive Behavior.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Medical malpractice disputes may affect physicians' well-being and clinical behavior. This study characterizes the medicolegal profile of malpractice disputes among Egyptian physicians practicing in Egypt and other Arab countries and examines how these disputes correlate with concurrent psychological, somatic, and defensive behavioral burdens. Methods: A cross-sectional online survey with nonprobability sampling was conducted from March to December 2025 among 586 practicing Egyptian physicians involved in at least one malpractice dispute. Participants completed the Kessler Psychological Distress Scale-6, the Impact of Event Scale-6, twelve items of the Defensive Medicine Behavior Scale, two items of the Malpractice Fear Scale, and a self-reported somatic symptom checklist. Multivariable regression identified independent correlates. Results: A lawsuit was the most serious dispute type for 51.4% of physicians, and management-related allegations were the most common (59.4%). Practice in Egypt rather than another Arab country was associated with procedure-related allegations (adjusted odds ratio 2.27; 95% confidence interval 1.49-3.45). Among resolved disputes, formal complaints (0.30; 0.18-0.49) and threats (0.45; 0.23-0.90) were less likely than lawsuits to end unfavorably for the physician. Recalling the dispute period, 62.3% had Kessler distress scores of 13 or more (mean 15.5 ± 6.4), with frequent post-traumatic stress symptoms (mean item score 2.7 ± 0.9) and somatic symptoms led by sleep disturbance (81.2%). High or very high defensive medicine scores were found in 92.0%. Conclusions: In this self-selected sample, malpractice disputes were associated with a heavy psychological, somatic, and behavioral burden. Medicolegal education, clearer complaint pathways, better documentation systems, and visible institutional peer support are policy considerations that need prospective evaluation.

papers.title: Shift Work and Acute Coronary Syndrome: Mechanisms, Modifying Factors, and Clinical Prevention.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Shift work causes recurrent circadian misalignment. This review synthesizes evidence linking shift work to acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and proposes a framework for prevention, return-to-work decisions, and future research. Methods: We conducted a narrative review using targeted searches of PubMed and major guideline repositories through July 2026. Search terms included shift work, night work, acute coronary syndrome, myocardial infarction, coronary heart disease, circadian misalignment, sleep, thrombosis, and cardiovascular risk. Revision-stage verification also examined atherosclerosis, coronary plaque, plaque vulnerability, and ischemia. Priority was given to prospective cohorts, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, controlled human studies, consensus statements, and major guidelines. Results: Night and rotating shift work are associated with a modestly increased risk of coronary heart disease (relative risk ~1.2-1.3), with duration-response gradients. Direct ACS-specific evidence is more limited but consistent with increased incidence and recurrence. Mechanistically, circadian misalignment and sleep deficiency promote autonomic dysregulation, hypertension, insulin resistance, dyslipidemia, inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, and atherosclerosis. Acute autonomic, hemodynamic, and prothrombotic changes may trigger plaque disruption or supply-demand ischemia. Risk modifiers include schedule intensity, cumulative exposure, chronotype, age, sex, comorbidities, sleep disorders, occupation, and health behaviors. Pregnancy is a specific evidence gap. Conclusions: Night and rotating shift work are probable contributory risk factors for ACS in susceptible workers. Clinical practice should integrate work schedule and sleep health into cardiovascular assessment, especially after ACS. Roster redesign offers the most defensible preventive strategy. Evidence that circadian interventions prevent ACS remains insufficient. More prospective ACS-specific studies are needed.

papers.title: Associations of Ultra-Processed Food Intake with Body Composition and Blood Pressure Across Sasang Constitution Types: A Prospective Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: High ultra-processed food (UPF) consumption is linked to adverse health outcomes. In Koreans, UPFs contribute approximately one-quarter of daily energy intake. We examined whether the longitudinal associations between UPF intake and changes in body composition, blood pressure (BP), and sleep parameters differ across Sasang constitution types (Taeum, Soeum, and Soyang). This prospective cohort study included 182 adults aged ≥30 years (baseline: 2015-2017; follow-up: 2019-2021). Dietary intake was assessed only at baseline using a 63-item food frequency questionnaire, and the percentage of total energy intake from UPFs (%UPF) was calculated. Multivariable linear regression models with baseline adjustment were used to evaluate longitudinal changes and interaction effects. In the Soeum type, higher %UPF intake was significantly associated with progressive longitudinal increases in weight (β = 0.27 kg, 95% CI: 0.08 to 0.46), and body mass index (β = 0.09 kg/m2, 95% CI: 0.02 to 0.16), and body fat mass (β = 0.15 kg, 95% CI: 0.00 to 0.30) per 1% increment in %UPF intake, with significant linear dose-response trends across tertiles observed only for weight and BMI (p for trend < 0.05). In the Soyang type, continuous %UPF intake was positively associated with systolic BP (β = 0.36 mmHg, 95% CI: 0.01 to 0.70). No significant longitudinal associations were observed in the Taeum type or for sleep parameters. Overall interaction terms between %UPF intake and constitution types were not statistically significant (all p for interaction > 0.05). In constitution-stratified analyses, higher %UPF intake was longitudinally associated with adverse changes in body composition in the Soeum type and in blood pressure in the Soyang type. Although overall interactions were non-significant, considering constitutional traits alongside dietary assessments may provide exploratory insights into cardiometabolic risk prevention.

papers.title: Pregnancy-Recognized Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Maternal-Fetal Outcomes: A Narrative Review of Gestational Rhinitis, Upper-Airway Mechanisms, and Treatment Evidence.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Pregnancy-recognized obstructive sleep apnea (POSA) is an operational construct, not a validated biological phenotype, and remains underrecognized in prenatal care. This review synthesizes evidence on POSA-related outcomes, evaluates gestational rhinitis as a candidate contributor to upper-airway vulnerability, and distinguishes pregnancy safety from demonstrated efficacy for OSA-related endpoints. Methods: This structured narrative review, informed by SANRA criteria, used a structured PubMed search (7 March 2026) with targeted supplementary searches through 9 October 2026, across six predefined domains. Results: Pregnancy-recognized OSA is associated in observational studies with hypertensive disorders, preterm birth, impaired fetal growth (in small pregnancy-specific studies), and severe maternal morbidity; residual confounding by obesity precludes causal inference. In a 2024 meta-analysis of randomized and observational studies (n = 809), continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) was associated with lower risks of gestational hypertension (RR, 0.65; 95% CI, 0.47-0.89) and preeclampsia (RR, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.50-0.98). Although secondary endpoints in individual trials suggested benefit, the pooled preeclampsia effect was fragile in sensitivity and subgroup analyses. Gestational rhinitis affects approximately one in five pregnant women and is a plausible but untested contributor to pregnancy-recognized OSA. Saline irrigation, budesonide (mainly inhaled-exposure data), and chlorpheniramine have gestational safety data, but the only randomized trial of an intranasal corticosteroid in gestational rhinitis was null, and we identified no study of OSA endpoints. Conclusions: Given the largely observational evidence, objective testing and individualized treatment may be considered in high-risk patients, pending adequately powered trials. CPAP is the standard treatment for objectively confirmed OSA.

papers.title: From Risk to Resilience: A Narrative Synthesis of Protective Factors and Proposed Mechanisms in Bias-Based Bullying Among Youth (2016-2026).
papers.abstract: Bias-based bullying (BBB) is a public health concern associated with psychological distress, suicidality, school disengagement, and other adverse health and developmental outcomes. This review synthesized empirical evidence on protective factors and examined proposed mechanisms and contextual conditions associated with how they operate. A theory-informed narrative synthesis was conducted using empirical studies published from 2016 through 2026 identified through APA PsycInfo, APA PsycArticles, ERIC, PubMed, Web of Science, and supplementary searches. Fifty-nine studies met the inclusion criteria and were appraised using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool. Findings were coded iteratively and interpreted through an integrated ecological and resource-based theoretical framework. Protective factors were identified across individual, interpersonal, and institutional levels. Individual strengths were more often associated with reduced harm than reduced exposure, whereas relational and institutional resources were more frequently associated with protective outcomes. Protective associations varied according to macro climate and policy context, intersecting identities and cumulative targeting, and proximal school and peer activation processes. No single factor was associated with protection for all youth, outcomes, or forms of BBB, and protective associations were often weaker under cumulative exposure. The findings suggest that protection depends on coordinated, accessible, and credible resources across ecological systems. Healthcare professionals should consider identity-based victimization when assessing youth with emotional distress, self-harm risk, disordered eating, sleep problems, or school disengagement, with attention to identity-responsive environments, accessible services, and coordinated follow-up.

papers.title: Multidimensional Frailty-Related Vulnerability Profiles Among Community-Dwelling Older Adults: A Data-Driven Cluster Analysis of the 2023 National Survey of Older Koreans.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Frailty-related vulnerability spans health, physical function, health behaviors, cognition, and psychological well-being. A single summary score may not fully convey how these features co-occur within individuals. This study identified data-driven frailty-related profiles among community-dwelling older adults and compared the magnitude of between-profile differences. Methods: We conducted a cross-sectional secondary analysis of the 2023 National Survey of Older Koreans. The analytical sample included 9950 participants. Ten indicators-self-rated health, chronic disease count, 1-year weight loss, sleep quality, weekly exercise frequency, fatigue, stair-climbing ability, 300-m walking ability, cognitive function, and depressive symptoms-were standardized and entered into K-means clustering. Candidate solutions for K = 2-10 were evaluated using within-cluster sums of squares and mean silhouette coefficients. Profile characteristics and effect sizes were compared using independent-samples t-tests, Pearson's chi-squared tests, Cohen's d, and Cramér's V. Results: The K = 2 solution had the highest mean silhouette coefficient (0.273) among the candidate solutions, indicating modest separation between clusters. Within the analytical sample, 6962 participants (70.0%) formed a lower-vulnerability profile and 2988 (30.0%) a multidimensional higher-vulnerability profile. The latter profile showed less favorable health, functional, psychological, and cognitive characteristics. Among the cluster-defining indicators, the largest descriptive differences were observed in 300-m walking (d = 2.013) and stair-climbing ability (d = 2.001). Conclusions: The two clusters represented a relative multidimensional vulnerability gradient rather than clearly distinct clinical phenotypes. Although the findings describe co-occurring vulnerability characteristics, their potential clinical utility requires independent and longitudinal validation.

papers.title: Symptom Networks in Patients Receiving Dialysis: A Systematic Review of Node Centrality, Bridge Centrality, and Methodological Quality.
papers.abstract: Patients receiving dialysis experience multiple interacting physical and psychological symptoms. Network analysis can identify symptoms occupying central or bridging positions, but findings across dialysis studies have not been systematically synthesized. This review aimed to synthesize central and bridge symptoms in adults receiving dialysis and evaluate the methodological quality of symptom network studies. Following PRISMA 2020 and a prospectively registered protocol (PROSPERO CRD420261410561), PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, CINAHL, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, and Wanfang Data were searched from inception to 9 May 2026. Two reviewers independently screened studies and assessed methodological quality. Centrality rankings from studies using the Dialysis Symptom Index or modified versions were min-max normalized and synthesized. Sixteen cross-sectional studies involving 7691 participants were included; 15 were conducted in mainland China and one in Singapore, while 14 involved hemodialysis populations and two involved peritoneal dialysis populations. Nine network models contributed to the centrality-ranking synthesis. Anxiety ranked first (median normalized rank 0.0690), followed by difficulty falling asleep (0.2353) and sadness (0.2400). Fatigue and irritability were most frequently identified as bridge or connecting symptoms. Thirteen studies reported strength correlation-stability coefficients of at least 0.50. Seven studies were rated low quality, eight moderate quality, and one high quality, with recurrent deficiencies in model-selection reporting, subgroup comparisons, raw centrality values, and uncertainty assessment. Psychological and sleep-related symptoms occupied prominent positions in the analyzed networks, while fatigue frequently connected symptom communities. The evidence predominantly reflects hemodialysis samples from mainland China. The applicability to peritoneal dialysis populations and to other healthcare systems and cultural settings remains uncertain. These cross-sectional findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation in more diverse populations.

papers.title: Long Sleep Duration and Multimorbidity in Older U.S. Adults: A Dose-Response Analysis of NHANES 2017-March 2020.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Sleep disturbance and chronic-disease multimorbidity are both common in aging populations, yet the dose-response shape of their association in U.S. older adults, and the sleep threshold of clinical relevance, remain unclear. Methods: We analyzed 2998 community-dwelling U.S. adults aged ≥60 years from the NHANES 2017-March 2020 pre-pandemic cycle. Self-reported sleep duration was categorized as short (<6 h), normal (6-8 h), or long (>8 h); multimorbidity was ≥2 of eleven physician-diagnosed chronic conditions. Survey-weighted logistic regression with jackknife variance estimated adjusted odds ratios (aORs), and restricted cubic splines characterized the dose-response shape. Results: Multimorbidity prevalence was 64.0%. The excess risk was confined to sleep of ≥9 h (aOR = 1.65, 95% CI 1.22-2.25); the band immediately above the reference, >8 to <9 h, showed no elevation (aOR = 1.08, 0.67-1.73), and the spline was J-shaped (P-nonlinearity = 0.005). Across the conventional >8 h category, long sleep was associated with multimorbidity (aOR = 1.41, 1.08-1.85, p = 0.014), whereas short sleep was not (aOR = 0.92, 0.58-1.47). This corresponded to an adjusted risk difference of 7.0 percentage points, and it was not materially attenuated by adjustment for a frailty phenotype (aOR = 1.38, 1.00-1.90) or among participants carrying at most one of the three available frailty criteria (aOR = 1.42, 1.03-1.97). The E-value, corrected for this common outcome, was 1.51. Conclusions: Long sleep, particularly ≥9 h, was associated with multimorbidity along a J-shaped dose-response. The association was moderate and the cross-sectional design cannot exclude reverse causation, so long sleep is best interpreted as a marker of accumulated disease burden rather than an actionable risk factor.

papers.title: Twenty-Four-Hour Movement Behaviors and Adult Mental Health: A Bibliometric Analysis of Global Trends, Research Hotspots, and Emerging Directions (2016-2026).
papers.abstract: Physical activity, sedentary behavior, and sleep constitute interdependent components of the 24-hour day and are jointly associated with mental health in adults. This study aimed to examine the global research landscape, hotspots, and emerging trends in this field from 2016 to 2026. Records published between 1 January 2016,and 30 April 2026, were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection. The bibliometrix package (version 5.3.0), implemented in R (version 4.5.2), was used to analyze publication and citation trends and contributions from countries, institutions, authors, and journals. Country-level publication output was quantified using full counting of unique document-country pairs, such that each publication was counted only once for a given country, whereas internationally co-authored publications were credited to all participating countries. Country citation rankings were determined by aggregating citations according to the corresponding author's country of affiliation. VOSviewer (version 1.6.20) was used to construct country-level co-authorship networks using full counting and to generate keyword co-occurrence networks. The R packages ggplot2 and circlize were used for additional visualizations, including chord diagrams of citation relationships among journals. A total of 527 publications were included. The annual global production from 2016 to 2026 reflected an overall upward trend with significant fluctuations. The amount of global output peaked in 2024 with 147 publications, whereas the number of total citations reached its highest in 2022 (2702). The United States was involved in 152 of the included publications, China in 118, and Australia in 87. Australia recorded the highest total citations (1757), followed by the United States (1667) and China (1556). Keyword overlay visualization revealed a shift from traditional behavioral epidemiology focused on workplace behaviors and subjective well-being toward integrated, precision-oriented mental health research emphasizing aging, cognitive health, circadian rhythm, and objective behavioral monitoring. Emerging hotspots included machine learning, compositional data analysis, isotemporal substitution, and accelerometer-based assessment. Research on 24-hour movement behaviors and adult mental health has evolved into an increasingly interdisciplinary field, with growing emphasis on integrated behavioral approaches, objective assessment methods, and healthy aging.

papers.title: Cardiovascular Comorbidity in Obstructive Sleep Apnea: The "Excessive Daytime Sleepiness" Phenotype Versus Comorbid Insomnia and Sleep Apnea (COMISA).
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS) and comorbid insomnia and sleep apnea (COMISA) are common clinical phenotypes of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). We compared their cardiovascular and metabolic comorbidity. Methods: Cross-sectional, single-center retrospective analysis of adults with polygraphy-confirmed OSA (apnea-hypopnea index ≥ 5 events/h). The EDS phenotype was defined as an Epworth Sleepiness Scale score ≥ 10 without insomnia (n = 54), and COMISA as OSA with clinically reported insomnia (n = 45). Multivariable logistic regression identified factors independently associated with phenotype. Results: OSA severity and the prevalence of any cardiovascular disease (90.7% vs. 86.7%) were similar. In the adjusted model, higher BMI (aOR 0.92 per kg/m2) and cardiac arrhythmias (aOR 0.20) were associated with lower odds of COMISA, and dyslipidemia with higher odds (aOR 2.51). Conclusions: Both phenotypes carry a high cardiovascular burden, but they seem to differ in metabolic profile: severe obesity and an arrhythmic tendency in sleepy OSA, and dyslipidemia in COMISA.

papers.title: Explainable Rhythm-Resolved EEG for Retrospective Comparison of Psychiatric-Service Adults with Recorded Violent Offences and Non-Clinical Controls.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: This study examines whether rhythm-resolved EEG features separate two retrospective groups and whether those features can be traced to explicit rhythms and sensors. The groups are psychiatric-service adults with recorded violent offences and non-clinical controls; the design does not compare offenders with non-offenders. Methods: We analysed 2554 non-overlapping 15 s EEG epochs from 95 adults (51 controls; 44 recorded-offence participants). RhythmFluxPat generated 9216 rank-transition features. CWImRMR selected 352 features with full-cohort labels, and classifier selection was nested within 95 participant-held-out leave-one-subject-out (LOSO) folds. Results: Classifier-nested tkNN classified 2392/2554 epochs (93.66%) and 93/95 participants (97.89%), and an independent check reproduced both confusion matrices. A nested support-vector machine (SVM) gave similar values (94.71% of epochs; 93/95 participants). In the comparative evaluation of four feature selectors, CWImRMR remained the best branch (93.85%), and a 44-feature subset reached 91.11%. DRLobish linked the selected features to delta and beta-to-gamma routes in the recorded-offence-assigned panel and to theta and alpha-to-theta routes in the control-assigned panel. Conclusions: RhythmFluxPat provides traceable rank-persistence and rank-exchange coordinates. The reported accuracies are optimistic internal estimates. Fully nested replication with matched psychiatric controls is required before any claim of generalisation or biomarker validity.

papers.title: Classification of Surface Electromyography Recordings from Young and Older Adults Using CWT Scalograms: A Window-Level Proof-of-Concept Study.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Age-related changes in skeletal muscle involve alterations in both muscle structure and neuromuscular function. Surface electromyography (sEMG) provides a non-invasive method for assessing muscle electrical activity. This study aimed to investigate whether time-frequency representations of sEMG signals combined with deep learning could classify recordings obtained from healthy young and older adults, without assuming that the discriminative features necessarily reflect age-related neuromuscular changes. Methods: sEMG signals were experimentally collected from 60 healthy adults, including 30 young and 30 older adults. The resulting continuous wavelet transform (CWT) scalogram images were randomly divided into training and test sets at the image-window level using an 80:20 ratio. Consequently, windows from the same participant could appear in both sets. Signals were filtered, segmented into overlapping windows, and converted into CWT scalogram images for classification using ResNet-18. Results: At the window level, the CWT-ResNet model achieved an accuracy of 78.98%, an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.8589, a sensitivity of 71.34%, a specificity of 85.06%, and a balanced accuracy of 78.20%. Muscle-specific analyses showed window-level classification accuracies ranging from 78.57% to 79.89% across all three muscle sites. However, the observed classification performance may have been influenced by differences in movement timing, active and resting periods, anthropometric characteristics, and participant overlap between the training and test sets. These potential influences were not isolated through additional control analyses. Conclusions: CWT-based time-frequency representations of sEMG combined with ResNet-18 demonstrated preliminary feasibility for classifying sEMG recordings obtained from young and older adults under the revised preprocessing and image-window-level evaluation conditions. The findings do not establish that the model specifically detects age-related neuromuscular changes. Participant-independent validation and analyses controlling for task execution and anthropometric characteristics are required.

papers.title: Subject-Specific Cardiovascular Signatures Revealed by Arterial Pulse Signals in Patients with Heart Diseases-Part I: General Cases.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: This study evaluates whether cardiovascular (CV) parameters derived from noninvasive arterial pulse signals can capture subject-specific physiological characteristics and longitudinal changes in patients with diverse heart diseases. Method: Arterial pulse signals at the radial artery (RA) and carotid artery (CA) of each patient were successfully recorded from all 18 patients using micro-fabricated tactile sensors. Signal quality was screened before analysis, and the accepted signals were analyzed using a single-degree-of-freedom time-frequency (SDOF-TF) framework. Key CV parameters, including time-based indices-heart rate (HR), heart rate variability (HRV), respiration rate (RR), and respiration modulation (RM), as well as harmonic amplitudes and normalized arterial pulse waveform (APW)-were extracted from measurements at rest and post-exercise across three rehabilitation visits in 18 patients with heterogeneous CV conditions. Longitudinal changes in CV parameters within subjects and variability between subjects were assessed. Results: Compared with a healthy reference, the patients exhibited heterogeneous CV profiles, with lower HRV in all patients except one with AF, who showed elevated HRV, and generally reduced post-exercise CV responses. Higher-order harmonic amplitudes were attenuated at the RA, while CA-derived APW measurements showed greater sensitivity to systolic upstroke slope. Marked inter-subject variability was evident in at-rest CV parameters and 5-min post-exercise responses. Longitudinal CV responses varied across rehabilitation visits, potentially reflecting multiple contributing factors. Conclusions: The 100% pulse acquisition rate supports the feasibility of the tactile sensor technology for pulse measurement, and the combined sensor technology and SDOF-TF framework enable quantitative characterization of shared and individualized CV patterns in cardiac patients and their post-exercise recovery, including time-based indices, harmonic signatures, site-specific differences, and interactions among CV parameters. These findings warrant further investigation in larger cohorts with appropriate physiological reference measurements.

papers.title: Breathing at a Distance: Telemedicine's Achievements and Pitfalls in Respiratory Disease Management-A Narrative Review.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Telemedicine (TM) has become an increasingly important tool in the management of respiratory diseases, offering the potential to improve access to care, support long-term monitoring, and reduce the burden of in-person visits. This narrative review aims to critically summarize the current evidence on the achievements and limitations of TM across major areas of respiratory medicine. Methods: A non-systematic search of PubMed and Scopus was performed for English-language studies published up to April 2026, using combinations of keywords related to TM, telemonitoring, and respiratory diseases. Relevant articles were selected based on their clinical relevance and contribution to understanding the role of TM in diagnosis, monitoring, and management, and additional studies were identified through manual screening of reference lists. Results: The TM has shown consistent benefit for objective, device-derived outcomes-most notably CPAP adherence in obstructive sleep apnea-and for process outcomes such as reduced travel burden and improved cost-effectiveness primarily demonstrated in obstructive sleep apnea and COPD, with limited systematic evidence of cost-effectiveness in interstitial lung disease, home mechanical ventilation, cystic fibrosis, and smoking cessation. However, evidence for hard clinical endpoints such as hospitalization and mortality remains inconsistent, and successful implementation depends heavily on the surrounding care model rather than on technology alone. Conclusions: The TM represents a valuable complement to conventional respiratory care with demonstrated achievements in adherence, patient satisfaction, and healthcare efficiency, but its adoption remains limited by heterogeneous evidence, workforce and resource constraints, and the risk of widening digital disparities. Larger, adequately powered trials with harmonized outcomes and sustained investment in integrated care pathways are needed to fully realize its potential.

papers.title: MTEP: A Matched Temporal Evaluation Protocol for Cognitive Fatigue Detection from In-Task Self-Reports.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Fatigue models are often trained on labels that participants produce, by an action, while the sensors record. We aimed to certify that an evaluation design's estimates reflect the state rather than the report. Methods: We present MTEP, a matched temporal evaluation protocol delivering label and feature separation, participant-level generalisation, within-recording position balance and report-independence, meaning that no window used to predict a report overlaps the act producing it. We certify report-independence by lead displacement and position balance with linear and nonlinear models, calibrate both certificates with injected effects of known amplitude and shape, compare four evaluation designs on corpora of known truth, and apply MTEP to CogBeacon and CL-Drive. Results: On corpora of known truth, MTEP returned the correct verdict in 78 of 80 cases against 58-62 for designs in current use, which concluded that a detector works in 16-19 of 20 corpora containing only the reporting act (MTEP: 1 of 20). The report-independence certificate had a specificity of 39/40 and detected an act-borne component of 0.05 local standard deviations in 30/40 replicates; the nonlinear position certificate detected imbalances the linear test missed (10/10 vs. 0/10). On CogBeacon, MTEP certified at a lead of one round, with pooled ROC-AUC 0.659 carried by task performance. Our model exceeded every published single-classifier accuracy on the same EEG features and protocols, yet a sensor-free clock matched or exceeded published accuracies on both corpora. Conclusions: Report-independence is a distinct requirement that existing designs do not imply; it can be checked from the collection protocol and certified on the evaluation sample.

papers.title: Postoperative Delirium Across the Perioperative Pathway: A Structured Narrative Review of Clinical Maturity and Implementation Priorities.
papers.abstract: Postoperative delirium (POD) is a highly prevalent but frequently underrecognized complication that disproportionately affects frail and older surgical patients. This structured narrative review aims to synthesize contemporary evidence on adult postoperative delirium across the perioperative pathway and to classify major preventive and therapeutic strategies according to clinical maturity, target population, and implementation readiness. A structured literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) and Web of Science Core Collection was performed, supplemented by ClinicalTrials.gov, official ESAIC and ASA resources, reference-list screening, and selected seminal pre-2021 publications. Current evidence supports a multifactorial model in which baseline cognitive and physiological vulnerability interacts with inflammatory, pharmacological, hemodynamic, nociceptive, sleep-related, and environmental stressors. No single anesthetic technique, processed-EEG target, blood-pressure threshold, cerebral oximetry strategy, or pharmacological agent consistently prevents POD across surgical populations. Multicomponent non-pharmacological prevention has the most consistent support, whereas dexmedetomidine and other pharmacological approaches appear context-dependent, and biomarkers and metabolic targets remain investigational. Future progress will depend on standardized delirium ascertainment, better phenotyping, multimodal prediction and prevention strategies, and reliable implementation systems that identify vulnerability early and maintain effective preventive care across transitions.

papers.title: A Hybrid Deep Learning Model (CNN-GRU) with MRMR for EEG-Based Depression Detection.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a prevalent mental health disorder for which objective and reliable diagnostic approaches remain an active area of research. Electroencephalography (EEG) has emerged as a promising non-invasive modality for identifying neural activity patterns associated with depression, while advances in deep learning have enabled effective analysis of complex EEG signals. Methods: In this study, we propose a hybrid deep learning framework that integrates convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for spatial feature extraction and gated recurrent units (GRUs) for temporal modeling of EEG signals. The spatial and temporal features extracted by the CNN and GRU components were concatenated into a 120-dimensional representation, after which minimum redundancy maximum relevance (mRMR) feature selection was applied to reduce redundancy and retain the 30 most informative features before classification. The proposed framework was evaluated using the publicly available MODMA EEG dataset, and its performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Results: Across 30 independent simulation runs, the CNN-GRU-mRMR framework achieved a mean classification accuracy of 96.74%, exceeding the performance of the comparison methods evaluated in this study. The model also demonstrated high precision, recall, and F1-score, indicating strong classification performance within the evaluated dataset. Conclusions: These findings suggest that integrating spatial and temporal feature learning with mRMR-based feature selection can improve EEG-based depression classification. Further validation using larger, more diverse, and independent clinical datasets is needed to establish the generalizability of the framework and evaluate its potential utility for objective EEG-based depression assessment.

papers.title: Subject-Specific Cardiovascular Signatures Revealed by Arterial Pulse Signals in Patients with Heart Diseases-Part II: Special Cases.
papers.abstract: Aim: This study evaluates whether cardiovascular (CV) parameters derived from noninvasive arterial pulse signals can reveal subject-specific characteristics in patients with atypical CV dynamics. Methods: Seven special-case patients-including a heart transplant (HTx) recipient and individuals with bradycardia (low heart rate, HR), low dicrotic notch (DN), and intermittent arterial pulse waveform (APW) variations-were analyzed across three visits over the cardiac rehabilitation (CR) period. Radial artery (RA) and carotid artery (CA) signals, acquired using micro-fabricated tactile sensors, were processed using a single-degree-of-freedom time-frequency (SDOF-TF) framework to extract multiple CV parameters. The analysis focused on descriptive characterization of subject-specific CV patterns in individual patients. Results: The patients exhibited highly heterogeneous CV profiles. Individuals with low HR exhibited relatively limited post-exercise HR changes. Individuals with low DN morphology exhibited elevated lower-order harmonic amplitudes. Individuals with intermittent APW variations exhibited cyclic changes in APW morphology at rest and during post-exercise recovery. Although CV patterns at rest differed across individuals, post-exercise assessment revealed more distinctive individual-specific differences, including differences between individuals within the same phenotype-based case subset. Across all patients and visits, RA measurements provided more stable and interpretable subject-specific CV patterns, whereas CA measurements were more susceptible to motion artifacts (MA) and sensor noise. For individuals with intermittent APW variations, the CA signals exhibited extremely poor signal quality, limiting their suitability for physiological interpretation. Conclusions: The SDOF-TF framework enabled the characterization of subject-specific, multi-parameter CV dynamics in these seven special cases. The findings illustrate the potential value of arterial pulse analysis for the individualized characterization of atypical CV dynamics. Future studies involving larger patient cohorts are needed to further investigate these findings and establish their clinical utility.

papers.title: Delayed Cerebral Ischemia as Progressive Neurovascular Unit Failure: A Hypothesis-Generating Perspective.
papers.abstract: Despite decades of investigation, delayed cerebral ischemia (DCI) remains the principal cause of secondary neurological injury following aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH). Successive paradigms including angiographic vasospasm, early brain injury, neuroinflammation, blood-brain barrier disruption, cortical spreading depolarization, microvascular dysfunction, oxidative stress, and metabolic failure have each explained important aspects of disease biology. However, these mechanisms have largely evolved as parallel explanations rather than components of an integrated model, leaving the dissociation between vasospasm and DCI, delayed onset, interpatient heterogeneity, and limited efficacy of vasospasm-directed therapies incompletely explained. This perspective proposes, as a hypothesis, progressive neurovascular unit (NVU) failure as a conceptual framework for DCI after aSAH. We integrate experimental, translational, and clinical evidence spanning vascular biology, neuroimmunology, cerebrovascular physiology, electrophysiology, metabolism, biomarker research, and therapeutic trials to develop a hypothesis-generating framework. The established mechanisms of DCI may represent interacting manifestations of progressive disruption of coordinated signaling among endothelial, vascular smooth muscle, pericyte, astrocytic, microglial, and neuronal compartments of the neurovascular unit. Within this framework, early brain injury may initiate NVU dysfunction, which is amplified by interacting vascular, barrier, inflammatory, electrophysiological, and metabolic disturbances, culminating in neuronal metabolic failure and tissue injury. Vasospasm is therefore positioned as one contributor to this process rather than a sufficient explanation for DCI. This framework offers a possible basis for interpreting clinical heterogeneity and therapeutic discordance while generating testable predictions for multimodal biomarker development, biological phenotyping, and mechanism-informed therapeutic strategies. The framework does not introduce new mechanisms; rather, it proposes a testable distinction between compensated NVU dysfunction and NVU failure, frames compartment-specific non-additive interactions as an empirical question, and organizes biomarkers by the NVU compartment they reflect. These proposals remain to be validated.

papers.title: Integrating Chronophysiological and Bioinformatic Perspectives on Nesfatin-1, Circadian Feeding Rhythms, and Cortisol Regulation.
papers.abstract: Nesfatin-1, a peptide derived from nucleobindin-2, regulates feeding, stress, and sleep-wake processes. To date, the available information suggests that nesfatin-1 is involved in stress regulation and colocalises with substances that influence cortisol, but the circadian interplay between nesfatin-1 and cortisol remains poorly defined. This review integrates biological timing, tissue-specific actions of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, and circadian misalignment, and is supported by in silico protein-association analysis. A structured database search retained relevant studies published from January 2006 to March 2026; heterogeneity necessitated narrative synthesis. Rodent experiments support effects of central NUCB2/nesfatin-1 on feeding and HPA-axis activation. Murine corticotroph experiments report increased POMC abundance, whereas an H295R human adrenocortical carcinoma-cell study reports reduced cortisol content and stimulated release. These findings concern different experimental systems and do not demonstrate coordinated central-adrenal regulation in vivo. The network analysis identified NPY and POMC as prominent nodes within the predefined candidate network, with enrichment of feeding- and HPA-axis-related pathways. Given the biologically targeted selection of input genes, these findings are interpreted as hypothesis-generating associations rather than independent confirmation of a regulatory mechanism. Within the literature examined in this review, direct evidence characterising the 24 h temporal profile of nesfatin-1 in humans, its phase relationship with cortisol, and potential alterations during circadian misalignment was not identified. This apparent evidence gap warrants further investigation through controlled, time-resolved human studies.

papers.title: Effects of BL Exposure on Circadian Rhythms and Rhythm-Related Disorders.
papers.abstract: Circadian rhythms represent a core physiological mechanism sustaining human physiological homeostasis and normal bodily function. Environmental light serves as a primary exogenous zeitgeber for circadian regulation. Among visible light spectral components, BL (BL) exerts a critical modulatory influence on the circadian system, with dual implications for physiological regulation and clinical intervention: excessive or inappropriately timed exposure may lead to circadian disruption, whereas appropriately timed BL interventions show potential to improve circadian alignment in selected populations. Accumulated evidence indicates that circadian disruption is associated with sleep disorders, mood disturbances, neurodegenerative disorders, as well as metabolic and immune dysfunction, and may have bidirectional relationships with disease progression. Nevertheless, most existing studies concentrate on circadian modulation by broad-spectrum light. Few efforts have synthesized the molecular mechanisms, potential disease-related pathways, and targeted intervention frameworks of BL-associated circadian disruption, and the translational potential of BL's bidirectional effects remains under-summarized, forming a prominent research gap. To fill this gap, this narrative review centers on the "BL-circadian rhythm-disease" regulatory axis. It outlines biological pathways in which circadian disruption may be implicated in multiple neurodegenerative disorders, highlights the circadian-modulating properties of BL, describes evidence linking inappropriate BL exposure to circadian disruption and disease onset or progression, and compiles clinical findings on BL-based interventions and their potential benefits for circadian function and selected disease-related symptoms. However, much of the evidence derives from observational studies and animal experiments, and a causal pathway linking BL exposure to disease through circadian disruption has not been definitively established. This review discusses the potential adverse and beneficial effects of BL in circadian disruption-related pathologies, addresses current research limitations, and offers theoretical references and fresh insights for mechanistic investigations, clinical research, and translational development of BL-targeted interventions.

papers.title: Biphasic Modulation of Absence Seizures by Lisuride in GAERS: Dissecting the Role of 5-HT2A Receptors.
papers.abstract: Serotonergic signalling modulates absence seizures, and activation of 5-HT2A receptors with TCB-2 suppresses spike-and-wave discharges in Genetic Absence Epilepsy Rats from Strasbourg (GAERS). We investigated the effects of lisuride, a serotonergic and dopaminergic ligand with low 5-HT2A receptor signalling efficacy, and examined the contribution of these receptors. Spontaneous seizures were recorded in freely moving male GAERS following systemic administration of lisuride (0.1 or 0.5 mg/kg), with or without pretreatment with the 5-HT2A receptor antagonist MDL11,939. Low-dose lisuride produced a modest pro-absence effect, whereas the higher dose produced a biphasic response: early seizure suppression followed by increased seizure activity. MDL11,939 did not abolish the early suppression, but the late increase observed with lisuride alone was not observed following pretreatment. These findings suggest that the early and late responses involve different mechanisms, with 5-HT2A receptors potentially contributing to the later phase. Lisuride's effects differ from those reported for the potent 5-HT2A receptor TCB-2, consistent with its broader receptor profile. Further work is needed to determine the contribution of its other targets, including dopaminergic receptors.

papers.title: Clinical and Genetic Spectrum of OPN1LW/OPN1MW-Associated Disorders in a Chinese Cohort: Contribution of Long-Read Sequencing.
papers.abstract: The highly homologous OPN1LW/OPN1MW gene cluster poses substantial challenges for molecular diagnosis. We retrospectively enrolled 12 male patients from 10 unrelated Chinese families with clinically suspected X-linked cone-opsin disorder, all of whom were confirmed to carry disease-associated variants or haplotypes in the OPN1LW/OPN1MW gene cluster. Clinical records, retinal imaging, electrophysiology, and available ocular biometry were analyzed together with short-read sequencing, Sanger validation, copy-number analysis, and Oxford Nanopore long-read sequencing for three cases with incomplete short-read resolution. Clinical subgroups included blue cone monochromacy (n = 5), X-linked cone dystrophy (n = 4), Bornholm eye disease (n = 2), and isolated color-vision deficiency (n = 1). Molecular results encompassed sequence variants, exon dosage alterations, a 51.8 kb deletion involving the locus control region, and exon 3 haplotypes. Long-read sequencing defined the deletion breakpoint in one case and the exon 3 haplotypes in two. In one boy with an X-linked cone dystrophy phenotype, the mean binocular axial length increased from 25.36 mm to 28.47 mm between 1.80 and 6.24 years of age. Our findings demonstrate the complementary utility of multimodal molecular assays and heterogeneous phenotypes of cone-opsin disorders, with sustained childhood axial elongation reported only as a single-case observation.

papers.title: Comparative Metabolomics Reveals L-Theanine as a Candidate Contributor to Cultivar-Specific Differences in PTZ-Induced Hyperactivity in Zebrafish.
papers.abstract: Hyperactivity and excessive neuronal excitation may lead to sleep disturbances and affect neurological health and overall quality of life, highlighting the need for safe, natural remedies. L-theanine, a natural bioactive compound in tea, has attracted interest for its potential effects on behavioral activity, although its effects on PTZ-induced locomotor responses in zebrafish remain unclear. Given the substantial variation in L-theanine accumulation among tea cultivars, we compared the metabolomic profiles of Camellia sinensis cultivars 'Baiye 1' (BY) and 'Longjing 43' (LJ43) and found that BY accumulated higher levels of L-theanine than LJ43. BY tea infusion exhibited stronger effects on pentylenetetrazole (PTZ)-induced hyperactivity in zebrafish, while LJ43 showed limited efficacy. Administering exogenous L-theanine, either alone or in combination with GABA or melatonin, alleviated hyperactivity and partially modulated the expression of gabra1 and mtnr1aa in zebrafish. Molecular docking revealed putative structural interactions of L-theanine with both GABRA1 and MTNR1AA, suggesting that GABA- and melatonin-related receptors may be involved in its attenuation of PTZ-induced hyperactivity. These findings highlight L-theanine as a potential contributor to the attenuation of PTZ-induced hyperactivity. Considering the complex composition of tea infusions, the distinct behavioral responses between BY and LJ43 may reflect the combined effects of multiple bioactive constituents, among which L-theanine may be one plausible contributor.

papers.title: Ion Channels and Transporters in Disorders of Glucose Homeostasis: From Molecular Mechanisms to Precision Medicine.
papers.abstract: Glucose homeostasis requires coordinated nutrient sensing, membrane excitability, hormone secretion, tissue glucose flux, and mitochondrial metabolism. Ion channels and transporters connect these processes, but mechanistic importance does not necessarily establish human disease causality or clinical actionability. This narrative review integrates human islet electrophysiology with glucose, metal-ion, and mitochondrial transport, distinguishing established causal human disease, replicated genetic susceptibility, limited genetic observations, human functional evidence, and predominantly experimental mechanisms. ATP-sensitive potassium (KATP) channel disorders provide the clearest bidirectional paradigm: activating KCNJ11 or ABCC8 variants can cause neonatal diabetes amenable to sulfonylureas, whereas inactivating variants cause congenital hyperinsulinism. Tissue-selective transporter syndromes, background potassium conductance, intercellular coupling, and organellar calcium handling illustrate additional mechanisms with different levels of human validation. Acquired remodeling in type 2 diabetes may be pathogenic, compensatory, or secondary to metabolic stress. We separate established management from investigational human replacement and preclinical targeting and critically assess functional assays, stem-cell models, transcriptomics, and genome engineering. Priorities are to resolve genotype-phenotype heterogeneity, establish causal direction and disease-stage dependence, and develop tissue-selective interventions with demonstrable patient benefit.

papers.title: Basolateral Amygdala Input to the Claustrum: Topology, Excitatory Synapse Properties and Cellular Targets.
papers.abstract: Although the claustrum (CLA) has been increasingly implicated in salience and attentional processing, its relationship with the basolateral amygdala (BLA)-a key structure for emotional valence-remains poorly defined. Here, we used viral tracing, optogenetics, and brain slice electrophysiology to characterize the spatial organization and function of BLA-CLA circuitry. We found a clear anatomical compartmentalization of axonal projections between the BLA and CLA within the ring-like outer shell of the CLA, with little axonal labeling in the CLA core. Given this anatomical segregation, it was surprising that optogenetic photostimulation of BLA axons produced comparable excitatory responses in neurons in both the CLA core and shell. Pharmacological experiments indicated that BLA axons make monosynaptic contact with both shell and core neurons, with the latter likely doing so via their distal dendrites that extend into the shell. When CLA neurons were stratified according to their projection targets, BLA axons overlapped more with CLA neurons projecting to the motor cortex than those projecting to the retrosplenial cortex. However, synaptic responses to BLA input were similar in CLA neurons projecting to both cortical targets. Our results provide the first functional characterization of a BLA input pathway that potentially carries valence-related signals to the CLA. Because the excitatory synaptic responses produced in CLA neurons by BLA input were small and subthreshold for action potential generation, our results also argue that the BLA input contributes to a broader convergence of excitatory inputs instead of being a primary driver of CLA activity.

papers.title: Disrupted Enteric Glial Cell Circadian Oscillation: A Proposed Mechanism Linking CMM-Axis Desynchronization, Gut Jet Lag, and Chronic Functional Constipation.
papers.abstract: Chronic functional constipation is highly prevalent and frequently recurrent, and gut jet lag triggered by circadian-rhythm disruption represents an important modern-lifestyle-associated risk factor. Although the Chrono-Microbiota-Motility (CMM)-axis conceptual framework for circadian-disruption-related functional constipation has been published, existing work mainly describes macroscopic microbiota-motility crosstalk and largely overlooks enteric glial cells (EGCs) as secondary peripheral circadian relays within the gut wall. Drawing on evidence from population-based epidemiology, human colonic specimens, multi-omics studies, and animal models of circadian disruption, this review delineates the pathological mechanisms by which disrupted circadian oscillations of enteric glial cells mediate hierarchical desynchronization of the CMM axis and contribute to gut jet lag. It further outlines a progressive pathological cascade from external circadian perturbations and enteric glial cell clock disruption to host-microbiota temporal desynchronization and subsequent collapse of the colonic motility network, discusses the potential implications of this mechanism for clinical risk stratification in chronic functional constipation, and provides a theoretical basis for future basic and translational research in gut chronobiology. It should be emphasised that the integrated mechanistic framework presented herein constitutes a testable hypothesis largely built upon pre-clinical animal observations and indirect human tissue evidence, rather than an established pathophysiological reality. This framework highlights one potential interstitial branch within the complex multi-cellular gut circadian regulatory network.

papers.title: Genome-Wide Analysis Reveals Copy Number Variation-Mediated Adaptive Evolution in Chickens Under Diverse Environmental and Domestication Pressures.
papers.abstract: To elucidate the genetic basis underlying chicken adaptation to diverse environmental selection pressures, this study performed a genome-wide analysis of copy number variations (CNVs) using publicly available whole-genome resequencing data from global chicken populations. Population differentiation (FST) and nucleotide diversity (π ratio) were integrated to identify signatures of selection associated with thermal adaptation, domestication, and high-altitude adaptation, followed by the identification of candidate genes and enriched biological pathways. In total, 6862, 9348, and 9384 high-confidence copy number variations (CNVs) were identified in the heat adaptation group, domestication group, and high-altitude adaptation group, respectively. Candidate genes associated with heat adaptation include AQP9, SLC4A8, CAT, SMPD2, and CLOCK, which are mainly enriched in biological processes related to water and ion homeostasis, antioxidant defense, and circadian rhythm regulation. Candidate genes related to domestication, such as IL18R1, HTR2C, GRIN2A, PRKAG2, and FABP1, are mainly involved in neuroactive ligand-receptor interaction, energy metabolism, immune regulation, and melanogenesis. In contrast, candidate genes identified in high-altitude populations include EDNRB, ITPR1, OGDH, PPARA, and ADCY6, which are significantly enriched in vascular smooth muscle contraction, the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle, the PPAR signaling pathway, and pathways related to hypoxic metabolic adaptation. The above findings indicate that distinct environmental selection pressures and artificial selection pressures have shaped population-specific CNV patterns in the chicken genome and promoted the formation of phenotypic adaptation through regulating water-salt balance, neural function, energy metabolism, vascular homeostasis, and hypoxic response pathways.

papers.title: Beyond Set Points: Rhythm-Based Detection of Change in Honey Bee Colony State from Hive Sensor Data.
papers.abstract: Disruption of daily patterns of activity, physiology, or social interaction is associated with stress and reduced fitness across species. In social insects such as honey bees (Apis mellifera), circadian organisation extends to the colony level, where rhythms emerge from interactions among individual clocks, hive conditions, and environmental cues. Precision apiculture offers a mature sensor toolkit for measuring colony-level variables, and several data streams carry early-warning information about colony condition. Almost all alarms, however, are triggered against set points rather than against the daily rhythm of the signal. We review each sensor technology to establish whether its data have been, or could be, analysed with a chronobiological lens, describing the measurement principle, the achievable temporal resolution and record continuity, the rhythmic signature expected on biological grounds, and any evidence that such a signature has been reported. We then use a synthetic dataset to illustrate the workflow: in this simulated example, rhythm metrics flagged a gradually developing decline approximately three weeks before a conventional threshold alert on the same data. This lead time is a property of the simulation and awaits validation on real colonies. Wherever continuous behavioural monitoring is deployed, rhythm-based metrics may offer a route to earlier, more interpretable detection of change than set point comparisons.

papers.title: Ligand-Specific Remodeling of the Anopheles gambiae RDL GABA Receptor by the A296S Mutation Differentiates Recognition of Fipronil and Fluralaner.
papers.abstract: The γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA)-gated chloride channel Resistance to Dieldrin (RDL) receptor is a major molecular target of insecticides, yet the structural basis by which resistance-associated mutations differentially influence chemically distinct ligands remains incompletely understood. Here, we investigated the effects of the classical A296S substitution on the interactions of the Anopheles gambiae RDL receptor with the phenylpyrazole fipronil and the isoxazoline fluralaner using homology modeling, molecular docking, 200 ns molecular dynamics simulations (apo receptors and three independent replicas of each ligand-bound complex), and MM/PBSA free-energy calculations that include an interaction-entropy (IE) term. Apo-state molecular dynamics simulations showed that A296S preserved the overall structural stability of the receptor while locally modifying the environment of the pore-lining M2 transmembrane helix. Although docking scored fluralaner more favorably than fipronil in both receptor variants, the replicated molecular dynamics simulations revealed ligand- and genotype-dependent behavior. In the wild-type receptor, fluralaner remained stably bound and had a favorable MM/PBSA free-energy estimate (-18.3 ± 4.2 kcal/mol), whereas the ligand RMSD of fipronil increased progressively and its estimate was close to zero (+1.2 ± 9.5 kcal/mol). In the A296S model, the fipronil estimate was similar (+1.6 ± 4.3 kcal/mol), but the fluralaner estimate became unfavorable (+10.0 ± 1.8 kcal/mol), and Ser296 itself contributed slightly unfavorably to both ligands. Together, these findings indicate that A296S does not act as a universal determinant of ligand recognition but is associated with ligand-specific changes in the modeled interaction landscape, with the larger predicted effect on fluralaner. These predictions derive from a homology model, were not tested by electrophysiology or binding assays, and do not measure functional resistance. They may nonetheless help inform the interpretation of cross-resistance patterns and structure-guided efforts targeting GABA receptor-based insecticides.

papers.title: Regional Arboreal Pollen Input and Its Millennial-Scale Variability Recorded in an Alpine Lake in the Hengduan Mountains, China.
papers.abstract: The Hengduan Mountains are a major hotspot for lake-sediment research, but regional vegetation responses to Holocene climate variability remain incompletely understood. Here, we analyzed pollen assemblages and concentrations from Dinggongniang Co (4633 m a.s.l.) to investigate regional vegetation-related changes over the past approximately 4.7 ka. Pollen percentage and concentration analyses were combined with ensemble empirical mode decomposition (EEMD) and Lomb-Scargle spectral analysis. Despite being located above the modern tree line, the lake sediments are dominated by arboreal pollen (89.5%), particularly Pinus, indicating substantial pollen input from lower-elevation forests. Total pollen concentrations were relatively low around 4.2 ka, increased markedly during the Roman Warm Period, and remained relatively elevated during the Medieval Climate Anomaly, suggesting changes in regional arboreal pollen input potentially associated with Asian summer monsoon-related hydroclimatic variability. Furthermore, time-series analyses identified a possible millennial-scale oscillation at approximately 1.3-1.4 ka, broadly consistent with variability documented in North Atlantic and Asian monsoon records. This finding highlights the value of high-altitude lake pollen records for tracing regional arboreal pollen input and suggests possible connections between Asian monsoon variability and broader Northern Hemisphere climate fluctuations. Although chronological uncertainties and multiple factors influencing pollen concentrations introduce some limitations, the observed patterns offer valuable insights into long-term vegetation-related environmental variability in the Hengduan Mountains.

papers.title: Hemodynamic spectral signatures across vigilance states: a whole-night EEG/fNIRS investigation.
papers.abstract: Sleep is accompanied by coordinated changes in neuronal activity and cerebral hemodynamics. However, cortical hemodynamic signatures across sleep stages remain poorly characterized, partly because most human electroencephalography (EEG)/functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) studies are limited in duration, rarely capture deep or Rapid-Eye-Movement (REM) sleep, have low sampling rate, or rely on a sleep-deprivation paradigm, which limits the generalizability of findings. Here, we combined whole-night polysomnography, EEG and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) in healthy young adults, as a bedside technology to monitor cortical hemodynamic fluctuations. We recorded fNIRS using an optimal, personalized, locally dense bilateral frontoparietal montage, alongside peripheral physiology recordings (respiration, photoplethysmography, mean arterial pressure). We computed oscillatory components of oxy- and deoxyhemoglobin (HbO-HbR) spectra across sleep stages using wavelet-based time-frequency analysis. Additionally, we analyzed within the same regions an independent sleep EEG-fMRI dataset (no REM recorded). Our results are suggesting that across frontal and parietal regions, slow-frequency (0.002-0.1Hz) power increased during N1 sleep in HbO and then progressively attenuated across N2 and N3 sleep, in HbO, HbR, and fMRI. REM showed a re-emergence of very-low-frequency power (<0.01Hz) in HbO and HbR. Higher-frequency oscillations (0.15-0.5Hz; overlapping respiratory-band) were selectively enhanced during NREM sleep (largest increase during N3) and returned toward wake-like levels during REM in frontal regions, with regional differences. Peripheral signals captured systemic physiology oscillations but did not reproduce the cortical stage-specific patterns. Together, our findings provide a cortical characterization of sleep-stage hemodynamic organizations that can serve as a reference for future mechanistic and clinical sleep studies.
